*The New Catalogue of the Zhenyuan Era*: *The Scripture on the Flower Garland of the Goddess Mārīcī*, one fascicle.
Translated by the Tripitaka Śramaṇa of Daxingshan Monastery, the Great Sage Amoghavajra, by Imperial Decree.
From the Newly Compiled Catalogue of the Zhenyuan Era: *The Scripture of Hārītī*, one fascicle. The title within the scripture reads:
*The Dhāraṇī Method of Hārītī*, translated by the Tripitaka Śramaṇa of Daxingshan Monastery, the Great Sage Amoghavajra, by Imperial Decree.
One fascicle on the Ritual for the Accomplishment of the Great Yakṣiṇī Mātṛkā Nandī and Her Beloved Son, also titled the Ritual of the Mother Haritī;
translated by the Tripiṭaka Master of Daxingshan Monastery, the Śramaṇa Amoghavajra, by Imperial Decree during the Zhenyuan era.
*Zhēnyuán Xīnrù Mùlù Zhòu Wǔshǒu Jīng* (One fascicle),
translated by the Tripitaka Master Xuanzang of the Great Tang;
included in the *Fàn jīng tú*.

Regarding the five dhāraṇī spells translated by Dan Chong: these are capable of extinguishing all sins. They are: (1) the Thousand-fold Dhāraṇī; (2) the Six-syllable Dhāraṇī; (3) the Divine Spell Spoken by Seven Koṭis of Buddhas; (4) the Divine Spell that Follows the Intent of All Tathāgatas; and (5) the Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva’s Spell according to One’s Heart. As for the Thousand-fold Dhāraṇī, there is also a separate transcription of it that exists as a distinct sutra within this collection; therefore, it is not listed separately here. It is incorrect for the *Datong lu* to divide these into five separate sutras.
The *Thousand-fold Dhāraṇī Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva Spell Sutra*, one fascicle, translated by the Śramaṇa Shi Zhitong of Zongchi Monastery during the Great Tang, was included in the *Shiyi*.

The second translation: The two *Sahasrāvarta* dhāraṇīs on the right are alternative translations of the same text as the *Sahasrāvarta Avalokiteśvara Dhāraṇī* at the beginning of the fifth fascicle of the *Saṃyukta Āgama* and the *Sahasrāvarta Dhāraṇī* among the miscellaneous dhāraṇīs.

*The Scripture on the Six-Syllable Divine Mantra* (or *The Ritual Method for the Six-Syllable Mantra*), one fascicle. Translated during the era of Empress Wu of the Great Tang by the Tripiṭaka Master Bodhiruci of India. Newly included in the canon. Fourth translation. The above scripture is a different translation of the same text as the "Mantra Method of Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva" and the "Scripture on the Five Mantras" found in the sixth fascicle of the *Collected Scriptures*, as well as the "Six-Syllable Dhāraṇī" within the *Various Mantras*.

*The Sūtra of the Great-Hearted Cundī Dhāraṇī of the Seven Koṭis of Buddhas*, one fascicle. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śubhakarasiṃha of Central India during the Great Tang Dynasty. Recorded in the *Dazhou Catalogue*. First Translation. *The Sūtra of the Great Radiant Dhāraṇī of the Mother of the Seven Koṭis of Buddhas*, one fascicle. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Vajrabodhi of Southern India during the Great Tang Dynasty. Newly included in the catalog. Second Translation. The above two sūtras are translations of the same original text with different renditions. Compared to the older and newer versions, they are somewhat more extensive; however, according to the Sanskrit manuscript, the translation is still not complete. Among the five principal dhāraṇīs and the miscellaneous dhāraṇīs, only the core mantras have been translated, with no other ritual methods provided.

*The Dhāraṇī Sūtra of the Mother of Seven Koṭis of Buddhas*, one fascicle. The title within the sūtra reads: *The Cundī Dhāraṇī Sūtra Spoken by the Mother of Seven Koṭis of Buddhas*. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master and Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of Daxingshan Monastery by imperial decree. Among the fifteen sūtras and twenty-eight fascicles newly entered into the *Zhenyuan Catalogue*, these are contained in three bundles: the first bundle contains seven fascicles, the middle bundle contains seven fascicles, and the final bundle contains fourteen fascicles.
The Newly Compiled Catalogue of Śākyamuni’s Teachings from the Zhenyuan Era, Scroll Twenty-one.
The Newly Compiled Catalogue of Śākyamuni’s Teachings from the Zhenyuan Era, Scroll Twenty-two.
Compiled by the Śramaṇa Yuanzhao of Ximing Monastery in the Western Capital.
There is a translation and a manuscript; it is recorded in the *Bodhisattva Tripiṭaka Catalogue* as one of the three major Mahāyāna sūtras translated both separately and in combination.

Below is the *Sūtra on the随心呪 (Heart-Mantra) of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva*, also titled the *Tārā-hṛdaya Sūtra*, in one fascicle. Translated by the Śramaṇa Zhìtōng of Zǒngchí Monastery during the Great Táng. Newly included in the catalogue. The aforementioned *Avalokiteśvara Heart-Mantra*:
The *Fivefold Sūtra of Previous Incantations*,
the "Initial Incantation of Avalokiteśvara" from among the *Miscellaneous Incantations*,
and the fifth fascicle of the *Collected Sūtras* were all previously translated.
Therefore, it is compiled here.

*The One-Scroll Ritual for the Practice of the Tathāgata Avalokiteśvararāja of the Vajraśekhara*, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master and Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of Daxingshan Monastery. Presented respectfully.
Imperial decree for the translation:
*Zhēnyuán xīnrù mùlù zhǒngzhǒng zázhòu jīng* (The Catalogue of Various Miscellaneous Dhāraṇī Sūtras Compiled in the Zhenyuan Era), one fascicle;
alternatively, the title lacks the character "jīng" (sūtra). Translated during the Northern Zhou dynasty by the Tripiṭaka Master Jñānagupta from India.

The *Shiyi* (Supplementary Collection) comprises twenty-three dhāraṇīs in total, including those translated by Danre: six dhāraṇīs from within the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra*; one "Dhāraṇī for Extinguishing Sin through Stupa Offerings"; one "Dhāraṇī for Extinguishing Sin and Being Welcomed by All Buddhas at the End of Life"; one "Dhāraṇī for Making Offerings to the Triple Gem"; one "Avalokiteśvara Repentance Dhāraṇī"; one "Vajra Snake Dhāraṇī"; one "Dhāraṇī for Stability in Seated Meditation"; one "Dhāraṇī for Swelling"; one "Dhāraṇī for Ghostly Illnesses"; one "Thousand-Turn Dhāraṇī"; four "Avalokiteśvara Heart-Dhāraṇīs"; one "Divine Dhāraṇī of the Seven Koṭis of Buddhas"; one "Dhāraṇī that Follows the Intent of All Tathāgatas"; five intermediate dhāraṇīs of the same source as the "Six-Syllable Dhāraṇī"; and one "Dhāraṇī for Taking Refuge in the Triple Gem."
*The Sūtra of the Supreme Dhāraṇī of the Buddha’s Uṣṇīṣa*, one fascicle;
translated by Du Xingyi, Court Gentleman of the Great Tang, by imperial decree;
recorded in the *Dazhou Catalogue*.
The First Translation of the *Buddhōṣṇīṣa-vijaya-dhāraṇī-sūtra*, one fascicle;
translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Divākara of Central India during the Great Tang Dynasty,
included here as a supplement.
The Second Translation of the *Buddhottamasikhā-uttaratantra-dhāraṇī-sūtra*, one fascicle;
translated by the Śramaṇa Buddhāpāli of Kapiśa during the Great Tang Dynasty;
recorded in the catalog of the Great Zhou.
The Third Translation: *The Sūtra on the Dhāraṇī of the Most Victorious Buddha-Uṣṇīṣa for Purifying Karmic Obstructions*, one fascicle.
Re-translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Divākara from Central India during the Great Tang Dynasty at the Eastern Capital;
appended as a supplement to the *Shiyi* (Supplementary Collection).
The fourth translation is the *Buddhoṣṇīṣa-vijaya-dhāraṇī-sūtra*, one fascicle (sometimes with the word "mantra" added). The five scriptures to the right are the same text translated differently.
The *Buddhoṣṇīṣa-vijaya-japa-vidhi*, one fascicle, has the title within the text: *Buddhoṣṇīṣa-vijaya-dhāraṇī-japa-vidhi*.
It was translated by the Tripitaka Master and Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of Daxingshan Temple by imperial decree.
*Vaiśravaṇarājāsūtra*, one fascicle.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master of Daxingshan Monastery, the Śramaṇa Amoghavajra, by imperial decree. Recorded in the *Zhenyuan xinding shijiao mulu*.
*Anantamukhasūtra*, one fascicle; also titled *Siddhādhigatamārajaya-sarvajñātāsūtra*. Recorded in the *Zhenyuan xinding shijiao mulu*.
Translated by the Upāsaka Zhi Qian of Wuchechi (Yuezhi) during the Wu Dynasty;
the first translation, titled *The Sūtra on Holding the Gate of Producing Immeasurable Doors*, in one fascicle, also known as the *New Sūtra on the Subtle and Secret Holding*.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Buddhabhadra of India during the Eastern Jin Dynasty.
The fifth translation is the *Ānandamukhanirhāradharmaparyāya*, one fascicle; alternatively titled *The Sūtra on the Holding of the Immeasurable Gateways*.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Guṇabhadra of India during the Song dynasty, it was subsequently included as a supplement.
6. *The Sūtra of the Dhāraṇī for Subduing Māra through Immeasurable Gateways*, one fascicle; alternatively titled *The Dhāraṇī for Subduing Māra*.
Translated by the Western Region śramaṇa Guṇabhadra and Xuanchang during the Song dynasty.
7. *The Ānandamukha-nirhāra-dhāraṇī-sūtra*, one fascicle.
The *Śāriputra-dhāraṇī-sūtra*, translated by the Indian Tripiṭaka Master Buddhayaśas during the Northern Wei Dynasty;
the eighth translation. One fascicle.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Saṃghavarman of Funan during the Liang Dynasty.
The ninth translation: *Ekottarika-bodhisattva-sūtra*, one fascicle;
translated by the Indian Tripiṭaka Master Jñānagupta and others during the Sui dynasty.
The ninth translation: *Anantamukha-nirhāra-dhāraṇī-sūtra*, one fascicle.
Translated by the Śramaṇa Shi Zhiyan of Zhixiang Monastery during the Great Tang Dynasty;

newly included in the catalog as the eleventh set of translations. The eight scriptures listed above are different translations of the same original texts. Among the records of the Chángfáng et al., there is additionally one scroll of the *Jue xian jing* (Sūtra of Jñānagupta), which is the *Chusheng wuliangmen jing* (Sūtra of the Birth of the Gate of Immeasurability). Furthermore, among the records of the *Gongde xian jing* (Sūtra of Guṇabhadra), there is one scroll of the *Chu wuliangmen chi jing* (Sūtra of the Immeasurable-Gate Dhāraṇī), which is the *Anantamukhanirhāradhāraṇī-sūtra*. Since these are duplicate entries, they are not preserved separately. Of the eleven new and old translations, three are missing from the original manuscripts.

*Chusheng Wubianmen Jing* (Sūtra on the Emergence of Boundless Gateways), one fascicle; the internal title reads *Chusheng Wubianmen Dharani Sūtra*. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master of Daxingshan Monastery, the Śramaṇa Amoghavajra, by imperial decree. *Zhenyuan Xinding Shijiao Mulü* (Newly Compiled Catalogue of the Teachings of the True Yuan Era). *Shengtang Biyin Dharani Jing* (Dharani of the Banner and Arm Seal of Victory), one fascicle. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang of the Great Tang, according to the *Neidian Lu* (Catalogue of Inner Scriptures). First Translation. *Miaobiyin Chang Dharani Jing* (Dharani of the Banner of the Wondrous Arm Seal), one fascicle. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda of Khotan during the era of Empress Wu of the Great Tang. Newly included in the catalogue. Second Translation. The above two sūtras are translations of the same original text with different versions. Regarding the *Shengtang Biyin Jing*, the old catalogues listed it as a single independent work; however, it has now been verified through examination as a duplicate translation.
The twenty-one sūtras above comprise twenty-one fascicles in one volume. *Anantapāramitā-dharmamukha-sūtra*, one fascicle; also known as the *Ananta-sūtra*.

Translated by the Śramaṇa Shi Shengjian of the Qifu Qin dynasty. First translation. *Ārya-jayavīrā-paripṛcchā-sarvadharmāpramāṇamukha-praveśa-dhāraṇī-sūtra*, one fascicle. Translated by the layman Tianyi of the Northern Qi dynasty. Third translation. The two sūtras above are the same text with different translations. Of the three successive translations, one is missing.
*The Vajra-Ayus-Dhāraṇī Sūtra*, one fascicle. The internal title of this scripture reads: *The Vajra-Ayus-Dhāraṇī Sūtra of All Tathāgatas*.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master and Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of Daxingshan Temple by imperial decree during the Zhenyuan era.
The *New Catalogue of the Zhenyuan Era* lists: *The Ritual for the Recitation of the Vajra-Ayus*, one fascicle. The internal title of this scripture reads: *The Dhāraṇī Recitation Ritual*.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa of Daxingshan Monastery, the Great Widely Wise Amoghavajra, by Imperial Decree.
*New Catalogue of the Zhenyuan Era*: *The Vajra-Supreme Flavor Dhāraṇī Sūtra*, one fascicle;
translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Buddhayaśas of India during the Northern Wei dynasty.
First Translation: *Vajramaṇḍala-dhāraṇī-sūtra*, one fascicle, translated by the Indian Tripiṭaka Master Jñānagupta and others of the Sui dynasty.
Second Translation: [Untitled]. The above two sūtras are different translations of the same original text.

*The Sūtra on the Adornment of the Bodhimaṇḍa*, one fascicle. The internal title of this sūtra reads: *The Dhāraṇī Sūtra on the Adornment of the Bodhimaṇḍa*. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master, the Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of Great Xingshan Monastery, by imperial decree. Included in the *New Catalogue of the Zhenyuan Era*. *The One-Syllable Uṣṇīṣacakravartin Sūtra Spoken at the Bodhimaṇḍa*, five fascicles. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master, the Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of Great Xingshan Monastery, by imperial decree. Included in the *New Catalogue of the Zhenyuan Era*. The above eight sūtras, totaling twelve fascicles, are contained in the same volume.
*The Sūtra of the Extraordinary Uṣṇīṣa*, three fascicles. The title within the sūtra reads: *The Sūtra of the One-Syllable Extraordinary Uṣṇīṣa, Chapter on Majestic Power*.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa Mahāprajñā Amoghavajra of Daxingshan Temple by Imperial Decree.

Recorded in the *New Catalogue of the Zhenyuan Era*: *The Ritual for Accomplishing Buddhahood through Simultaneous Recitation of the Yoga of the One-Syllable Wheel King from the Vajraśekhara Sūtra*, one fascicle.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of Great Xingshan Monastery by Imperial Decree;
*The Sūtra of the Questions of the Bodhisattva Siṃhavikrāmin*, one fascicle, translator lost; included in the New Catalogue of the Zhenyuan Era.
Now appended to the Eastern Jin Records: *The Dhāraṇī Sūtra of the Flower Accumulation*, one fascicle;
translator lost, now appended to the Eastern Jin Records. *The Divine Dhāraṇī Sūtra of the Flower Treasury*, one fascicle.

Translated by the Yuezhi Upāsaka Zhi Qian of the Wu [Dynasty]. It is erroneously included in the Zhou [Catalogue] among the single-text editions. The above three sūtras are translations of the same original text with different versions;

their chronological order cannot be distinguished. *Six-Character Mantra-King Sūtra*, one fascicle. Translator lost. Now appended to the Eastern Jin Catalogue. First Translation. *Six-Character Divine Mantra-King Sūtra*, one fascicle. Translator lost. Included in the *Shiyi* (Supplement). Second Translation. The above two sūtras are translations of the same original text with different versions.

*The Sūtra on the Questions of the Bodhisattva Gaganagañja*, one fascicle; also titled *The Sūtra on the Dhāraṇī Mantra of the Seven Buddhas Asked by the Bodhisattva Gaganagañja*. Translator lost. Now appended to the Liang Record; included in the *Shiyi* (Supplementary Collection). First translation: *The Sūtra on the Tathāgata’s Skillful Means and Mantras*, one fascicle. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Jñānagupta of India during the Sui Dynasty, etc. Second translation. The above two sūtras are the same text with different translations.
Regarding this *Tathāgata-upāya-sūtra*, the old catalog records it as a single-text edition, while the new examination identifies it as a retranslation.

*The Scripture on the Dhāraṇī-Mantra of Holding Phrases*, one fascicle; also titled *The Dhāraṇī Phrases*. Translated by the Yuezhi Upāsaka Zhi Qian of the Wu [Dynasty]. Included in the *Shiyi* (Supplementary Collection). First translation. *The Scripture on the Dhāraṇī-Pātra*, one fascicle; also called *The Dhāraṇī-Pātra Mantra*. Translated by the Śramaṇa Zhu Tanwulan of the Western Regions during the Eastern Jin [Dynasty]. Included in the *Shiyi*. Second translation. *The Scripture on the Tathāgata Supreme Lamp King of the East*, one fascicle. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Jñānagupta and others of India during the Sui [Dynasty]. Recorded in the *Neidian Lu* (Inner Canon Catalogue). Fourth translation. The above three scriptures are different translations of the same original text. The first two versions are abbreviated, while the latter scripture is somewhat more extensive. Of the four translations, two are extant and one is missing. Regarding the *Scripture on the Supreme Lamp King*, the old catalogues list it as a single, independent work, whereas a new examination has determined it to be a re-translation.

*The Sūtra of the Dhāraṇī-mantra of Skillful Means*, one fascicle; translator lost, now appended to the catalogue of the Eastern Jin. *The Sūtra of the Dhāraṇī of the Secret Gate of Vajra*, one fascicle; translator lost, now appended to the catalogue of the Eastern Jin. *The Sūtra of the Divine Mantra of the Dharma-gate for Protecting Life*, one fascicle; translated during the reign of Empress Wu by the Indian Tripiṭaka Master Bodhiruci; included in the *Da Zhou Catalogue*. Third translation. These three sūtras share the same original text but differ in translation. As for the first two sūtras, it is impossible to determine which precedes the other. Furthermore, the entry for the *Sūtra of the Dharma-gate for Protecting Life* in the *Da Zhou Catalogue* is erroneously listed among the single-text translations.

*The Sutra of the Vimalaprabhāsa-mahādhāraṇī*, one fascicle. Translated during the era of the Great Tang Empress by the Śramaṇa from the Western Regions at Mito Mountain Temple; newly included in the canon as the second translation. Furthermore, the Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda of Khotan previously translated it under the title *The Dhāraṇī of the Stainless Pure Light Sutra*, but as the original manuscript has not yet been recovered, that version is omitted. The sixteen aforementioned sutras, totaling eighteen fascicles, constitute a single volume.
*The Scripture on the Dhāraṇī for Requesting Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva to Eliminate and Subdue Poisonous Harm*, one fascicle; also simply titled *The Scripture on Requesting Avalokiteśvara*.
Translated by the foreign lay devotee Zhu Nanti during the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Of two translations, one is missing. *The Scripture on the Girl Xiangyuli*, one fascicle; the title within the scripture adds the words "Spoken by the Buddha."
*The Dhāraṇī Sūtra for Eliminating All Diseases*, one fascicle, translated by the Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa of Daxingshan Monastery, the Great Widely Wise Amoghavajra, by imperial decree;
newly compiled and included in the catalog during the Zhenyuan era.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa of Daxingshan Monastery, the Great Widely Wise Amoghavajra, by imperial decree.
*The Dhāraṇī Sūtra for Being Able to Purify All Eyes*, one fascicle. The title within the sūtra reads *The Dhāraṇī Sūtra for Being Able to Purify All Eye Diseases*.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master and Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of Da Xingshan Monastery by imperial command;
recorded in the *New Catalogue of the Zhenyuan Era*. *The Dhāraṇī Sūtra of Raining Jewels*, one fascicle. The title within the sūtra has been augmented with the words "Spoken by the Buddha."
Translated by the Tripitaka Śramaṇa of Daxingshan Monastery, the Great Widely Wise Amoghavajra, by Imperial Decree.

*The Ritual for the Recitation and Accomplishment of the Offering to the Bodhisattva Amṛtakuṇḍalī*, one fascicle. The title within the scripture reads: *The Ritual for the Recitation and Accomplishment of the Offering to the Bodhisattva Amṛtakuṇḍalī*, translated by the Tripitaka Śramaṇa of Daxingshan Monastery, the Great Widely Wise Amoghavajra, by Imperial Decree.
*The Newly Compiled Catalogue of the Zhenyuan Era*, Fascicle One.
*The Scripture on the Dhāraṇī of the One-Braided Honored One Spoken by the Buddha*, one fascicle.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master and Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of Daxingshan Monastery by imperial decree during the Zhenyuan era.

*The Ritual Manual for the Recitation of the Greatly Efficacious and Accomplished King of Holy Yamāntaka’s Wrathful Power*, one fascicle. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master and Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of Daxingshan Monastery by imperial decree during the Zhenyuan era.
Translated by the Tripitaka Śramaṇa of Daxingshan Monastery, the Great Widely Wise Amoghavajra, by Imperial Decree.
*The Method of the Kāpālika-Aveśa Spoken by the Deva Maheśvara: A Ritual for Swift Manifestation of Efficacy*, one fascicle.
Translated by the Tripitaka Śramaṇa of Daxingshan Monastery, the Great Widely Wise Amoghavajra, by Imperial Decree.
*The Ritual of the Great Sage Tianhuānxi (Heavenly Joy) Double-Body Vināyaka*, one fascicle.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master and Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of Daxingshan Temple by imperial decree.
The eleven sūtras and eleven fascicles listed above in the *New Catalogue of the Zhenyuan Era* constitute a single volume.
*Neizang baibao jing* (Sutra of the Inner Treasury of a Hundred Jewels), one fascicle; also titled *Neizang baipin jing* (Sutra of the Inner Treasury of a Hundred Chapters).
Translated by the Yuezhi Tripiṭaka Master Zhi Loujiachen of the Later Han Dynasty;
the first translation.
Of the two translations, one lacks the *Wenshi xiyu zhong seng jing* (One Scroll;
also simply titled *Wenshi jing*), translated by the Anxi Tripiṭaka Master An Shigao of the Later Han Dynasty and included in the *Shiyi*.

Of the first and second translations, one version lacks the *Xulai jing* (One Scroll), translated by the Yuezhi Upāsaka Zhi Shilun of the Former Liang. Of the third translation and the preceding two, three versions lack the *Sihemai jing* (One Scroll)—also known as the *Pusa daoshu jing* or the *Daoshu sanmei jing*.
Translated by the Upāsaka Zhi Qian of Yuezhi during the Wu Dynasty;
the first of two translations, one of which is missing:
*Bodhisattvajanmabhūmi-sūtra* (also known as the *Carmamagha-sūtra*), one fascicle.

Translated by the Wu-period Yuezhi Upāsaka Zhi Qian; the Zhou period version is a single-text edition with errors. First translation: *The Sūtra on the Four Unobtainables*, one fascicle, translated by the Western Jin Tripiṭaka Master Dharmarakṣa.
Second translation: [one of the two translations is missing]. *The Sūtra of the Brahmin Woman Śiri*, one fascicle—also known as *The Sūtra of the Woman Śiri*; the other translation is missing.

*Chengju guangming dingyi jing* (Sūtra on the Samādhi of Perfect Radiance), one fascicle—also known as *Chengju guangming sanmei* or simply *Chengju guangming jing*. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Zhu Fahu of the Western Jin; the first of two translations, the second being lost.

*Baowang jing* (Jewel Net Sūtra), one fascicle—also known as *Baowang tongzi jing* (Jewel Net Boy Sūtra). Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Zhi Yao of the Western Regions during the Later Han; the first of two translations, the second being lost.

*Bodhisattvaxing wushi yuan shen jing* (Sūtra on the Fifty Causes and Conditions of the Bodhisattva’s Practice), one fascicle. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Zhu Fahu of the Western Jin; the first of two translations, the second being lost.

*The Sūtra on the Bodhisattva’s Practice*, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin (First Translation); also known as *The Sūtra on the Elder Vaiśya’s Inquiry into the Contemplation of Physical Conduct*, translated by the Śramaṇa Bai Fazang of Henei during the Western Jin (Second Translation).
Of these three translations, two are missing. *The Sūtra on the Fields of Merit for the Virtuous*, translated jointly by the Śramaṇas Fa-li and Fa-ju of the Western Jin (Third Translation).

Of these three translations, two are missing. Also referred to as *The Sūtra on All Fields of Merit* or simply *The Sūtra on the Fields of Merit*. *The Mahāvaipulya Tathāgatagarbha Sūtra*, one fascicle.

Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Buddhabhadra of India during the Eastern Jin Dynasty; the third translation (of which two others are missing). *The Mahāvaipulya Tathāgatagarbha Sūtra*, one fascicle.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of Daxingshan Temple by imperial decree.
*The Sūtra of the Buddha’s Words*, one fascicle, newly entered into the Zhenyuan Catalogue.
*The Sūtra of King Suvarṇavarṇa*, one fascicle. Translated by the Indian Tripiṭaka Master Bodhiruci during the Northern Wei dynasty;

the first of two translations, the second being missing. *The Sūtra on the Exposition of the Deeds of the Laity and the Clergy*, one fascicle. Translated by the Brahmin Gautama Prajñāruci during the Northern Wei dynasty;

the second of two translations, the first being missing. *The Sūtra of the Names of One Hundred Buddhas*, one fascicle. Translated by the Śramaṇa Shi Shengjian during the Qifu Qin dynasty; the second of two translations, the first being missing.

Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Narendrayaśas of India during the Sui Dynasty; this is the second translation. Of the two translations, one lacks the first eighteen sūtras. The eighteen fascicles are contained in a single volume.
*Chengyang zhufu gongde jing* (Sūtra on Praising the Merits of All Buddhas), three fascicles; also titled *Jizhufu hua* (Flowers of All Buddhas Collected), or four fascicles.

Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kiṅkara of the Western Regions together with Tanyao during the Northern Wei dynasty. This is the third translation; two of the three translations are missing. *Suzhenti tianzi jing* (Sūtra of the Son of Heaven Suśīma), three fascicles; also called *Wensishi jing* (Sūtra on Asking about Four Matters), or two fascicles.

Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin dynasty. This is the first translation; one of the two translations is missing. *Mahāmāyā sūtra*, one fascicle; also simply called *Māyā jing*, or two fascicles.

*The Scripture on Removing Fear of Calamities*, one fascicle, translated by the Śramaṇa Shi Tanyǐng of the Qi dynasty; second translation, one version missing. Translated by the Śramaṇa Shi Shèngjiān of the Qifu Qin dynasty;
second translation, one version missing. *The Pí Scripture*, one fascicle, also known as the *Pí Scripture Excerpt*, translated by the Upāsaka Zhīqián of Yuezhi during the Wu dynasty;

included in the *Shiyí* (Supplement) collection; second translation, with three versions in total, two of which are missing. *The Scripture on the Prophecy of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva*, one fascicle, also titled *The Scripture on the Prediction for Avalokiteśvara*.

Translated by the Song dynasty monk Śramaṇa Dharmodgata (Tánwújié); third translation. Two translations are missing. *The Sūtra on the Prophecy of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva*, one fascicle. The internal title of the sūtra reads: *The Thirty-first Chapter on the Prophecy of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva from the Buddha-spoken Mahāvaipulya Mañjuśrī Sūtra*.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of Daxingshan Temple by imperial decree.
The seven sūtras totaling eleven fascicles listed above in the *New Catalogue of the Zhenyuan Era* are contained in the same volume.
*The Sutra of the Dragon King of the Sea*, four fascicles (or three fascicles), translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin;

of these two translations, one lacks the beginning. *The Śūraṅgama Samādhi Sūtra*, three fascicles (also called the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*), or two fascicles, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kumārajīva of the Yao Qin;

of the nine translations, eight are missing. *The Sutra on the Method of Practicing the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra’s Conduct*, one fascicle, which also appears within the *Sutra of Profound Merit*; it is also called the *Samantabhadra Contemplation Sūtra*.

*The Sutra on the Contemplation of the Two Bodhisattvas Bhaiṣajyarāja and Bhaiṣajyasamudgata*, one fascicle, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmamitra of Kasmīra during the Song dynasty; the third translation, two other translations being missing.
*The Sutra on the Questions of the Bodhisattva Acintya*, also titled *The Sutra Spoken [by the Buddha]*, one fascicle, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kumārajīva of the Yao Qin dynasty;
the second translation, two other translations being missing. The above five sutras comprise ten fascicles and are contained in the same volume.

*The Scripture on the Ten Abodes for Severing Bonds*, ten fascicles (alternatively titled *The Scripture on the Ten Stages for Severing Bonds*; also in eleven or fourteen fascicles). Translated by the Śramaṇa Zhu Fonian of Liangzhou during the Yao Qin dynasty. This is the second translation; the first translation is missing. *The Essential Collection of All Buddhas*, two fascicles (also simply titled *The Essential Collection*). Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Zhu Fahu of the Western Jin dynasty. This is the first translation; the second translation is missing. *The Scripture on Unprecedented Causes and Conditions*, two fascicles (also simply titled *The Unprecedented Scripture*). Translated by the Śramaṇa Shi Tanjing of the Xiao Qi dynasty. This is the second translation; the first translation is missing. The above three scriptures comprise fourteen fascicles in two volumes.

*The Bodhisattva’s Necklace Sūtra* (Pusa yingluo jing), twelve fascicles, or fourteen fascicles, or sixteen fascicles; translated by the Śramaṇa Zhu Fonian of Liangzhou during the Yao Qin dynasty. Second translation. One of the two translations is missing. *The Sūtra on the Samādhi of Surpassing the Sun’s Radiance* (Chaoriming sanmei jing), two fascicles; or without the word "samādhi. Translated by the lay devotee Nie Chengyuan of the Western Jin dynasty. Second translation. One of the two translations is missing. The above two sūtras comprise fourteen fascicles in two volumes.

The *Bhadrapāla-kalpa-sūtra* (賢劫經), thirteen fascicles—also known as the *Bhadrapāla-samādhi-sūtra* (颰陀三昧經)—in either seven or ten fascicles, one set; translated by the Tripitaka Master Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin. Of the two translations, one is missing. From the *Vimalaprabhā-dhāraṇī-sūtra* (無垢淨光陀羅尼經) below, thirty-six sūtras, though said to be re-translations, [are included].
Only one copy remains; all others have been lost and cannot be found despite diligent search. *Mahāyāna Sūtras Translated Singly*:

One hundred and thirty-one works in two hundred and ninety-three fascicles, arranged in twenty-four bundles. 1. *Dharmolkā-dhāraṇī-sūtra*, twenty fascicles (two bundles). Translated by the Indian Tripiṭaka Master Jñānagupta and others of the Sui Dynasty. 2. *Mahātejas-dhāraṇī-sūtra*, twenty fascicles (two bundles). Translated by the Indian Tripiṭaka Master Jñānagupta and others of the Sui Dynasty. 3. *Buddhanāma-sūtra*, twelve or thirteen fascicles. Translated by the Indian Tripiṭaka Master Bodhiruci of the Northern Wei Dynasty. 4. *Sūtra of the Names of Three Thousand Buddhas of the Three Kalpas*, three fascicles. 5. *Sūtra of the Thousand Buddhas of the Past Adorned Kalpa*, first fascicle.
The *Sūtra of the Names of the Thousand Buddhas of the Present Bhadrakalpa*, Middle Fascicle;
and the *Sūtra of the Names of the Thousand Buddhas of the Future Nakṣatra-kalpa*, Lower Fascicle (translator lost).
These were included in the *Shiyi* (Supplementary Collection) and are now appended to the Liang dynasty catalog.
The above two sutras comprise fifteen fascicles in two volumes.

Regarding the *Names of Buddhas of the Three Kalpas*, it was compiled into a single work from the *Chángfáng Rùzàng Lù* (Record of Works Admitted into the Canon by Chángfáng); among these, the *Names of Buddhas of the Bhadrakalpa* is derived from the *Bhadrakalpika-sūtra*.
These have been combined into a single retranslation.
Now, as the aforementioned lists of Buddha names constitute their original individual versions,
they are compiled here according to their respective categories.

*The Sūtra of the Names of Five Thousand Five Hundred Buddhas*, eight fascicles; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Jñānagupta and others of Central India during the Sui dynasty. *The Sūtra on the Inconceivable Merits and the Protection of All Buddhas*, two fascicles—also recorded as four fascicles in the *Catalogue of All Scriptures* (*Chu zhong jing mu*)—translated anonymously during the Cao Wei period and included in the *Supplement to the Tripiṭaka* (*San zang shi yi*). These two sūtras comprise ten fascicles in total and are kept in the same volume. Regarding the *Sūtra on Inconceivable Merits*, the *Record of the Great Zhou* (*Dazhou lu*) states that it is the same text as the *Sūtra of the Questions of the Bodhisattva of Inconceivable Merits*; this is an error.

*The Flower Hand Sūtra* (Huáshǒu jīng), thirteen fascicles—also known as *The Sūtra Collecting All Roots of Goodness* (Shè zhū shàngēn jīng)—or eleven or twelve fascicles in one bundle; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kumārajīva of the Yaoqin [Dynasty]. *The Mahāvaipulya Dhāraṇī Sūtra* (Dàfāngděng tuóluóní jīng), four fascicles—also known as *The Vaipulya Tandi Dhāraṇī Sūtra*; translated by the Śramaṇa Fǎzhòng of the Northern Liáng at Gāochāng Commandery. According to the *Bǎochàng Lù*, this is the *Saṃghāṭa Sūtra* in four fascicles. *The Sūtra on the Samādhi of Power Adornment* (Lì zhuāngyán sānmèi jīng), three fascicles; translated by Prince Yuépóshǒuná of the Kingdom of Ujjayinī during the Yuánwèi [Dynasty]. *The Mahāvaipulya Perfect Enlightenment Sūtra of Definitive Meaning* (Dàfāngguǎng yuánjué xiūdúoluó liǎoyì jīng), one fascicle; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Nālandiyāśas of India during the Sui [Dynasty]. Translated by the Śramaṇa Buddhatoṭara of Kasmira during the Dàtáng [Dynasty]. These four aforementioned sūtras, totaling twelve fascicles, are compiled together in one bundle as supplementary additions.

*The Scripture on the Ocean-like Samādhi of Contemplating the Buddha*, ten fascicles (or eight fascicles), one volume; alternatively, the title lacks the character "Ocean" (*hai*). Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Buddhabhadra of India during the Eastern Jin dynasty.

Regarding this *Scripture on the Samādhi of Contemplating the Buddha*, the *Catalogue of the Great Zhou* (*Da Zhou lu*) states it was translated by Guṇabhadra during the Yongchu era of the Song dynasty. However, the *Catalogue of Inner Scriptures* (*Neidian lu*) notes that it was actually translated by Juexian of the Eastern Jin, and not by Guṇavarman of the Song; thus, the *Great Zhou Catalogue* is in error. Furthermore, it states that this work is the same text as the single-fascicle *Scripture on the Samādhi of Contemplating the Buddha* translated by Kumārajīva of the Later Qin, compiled here as a duplicate translation. Since the version translated by Master Kumārajīva has long been lost and its fascicle count differs entirely, they cannot be directly correlated. For now, I have followed various ancient catalogues and included it within the single-fascicle section. *The Great Skillful Means: The Sūtra on the Buddha’s Requital of Kindness*, seven fascicles; translator lost.
The *Bodhisattvapūrvakarmasūtra* in three fascicles from the Later Han records has a lost translator;

it is now appended to the "Supplementary Collection" (Shiyi) of the Eastern Jin. These two aforementioned scriptures comprise ten fascicles in one volume. According to the *Dazhou lu*, the seven-fascicle *Baoen jing* is said to be a translation from the Han dynasty, sharing the same root text as the single-fascicle *Dafangbian baoen jing*. Furthermore, the three-fascicle *Bodhisattvapūrvacaryā-sūtra* is said to share the same root text as the single-fascicle *Bodhisattvapūrvacaryā-sūtra* translated by Nie Daozhen of the Western Jin. However, since the single-fascicle versions of the *Baoen* and *Pūrvacaryā* sūtras were previously missing and their fascicle counts differ significantly, they cannot be cross-referenced or paired. Therefore, they are here compiled within the single-fascicle section according to various older catalogs.

*The Scripture on the Collection of Dharmas*, six fascicles (or seven fascicles), translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Bodhiruci of India during the Northern Wei dynasty; *The Scripture on the Contemplation of the Practice of All Dharmas*, four fascicles, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Jñānagupta and others of India during the Sui dynasty. These two scriptures comprise ten fascicles in one volume.

The *Bodhisattva Dwelling in the Womb Sūtra* (*Pusa chutai jing*), five fascicles—also simply called the *Womb Sūtra* (*Tai jing*) or eight fascicles—translated by the Śramaṇa Zhu Fonian of Liangzhou during the Yao Qin dynasty. The *Sūtra on the Samādhi of Extensively Manifesting the Propagation of the Way* (*Hongdao guangxian sanmei jing*), four fascicles; sometimes the word "samādhi" (*sanmei*) is omitted. It is also titled the *Anavatapta Dragon King Sūtra* (*A-nu-da longwang jing*) or the *Sūtra on Entering the Vajra Gate through Concentrated Mindfulness* (*Ru jin'gangmen dingyi jing*). It consists of twelve chapters and was translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Zhu Fahu of the Western Jin. Regarding the above sūtra, the *Renshou*, *Dazhou*, and other catalogs all state that it is a different translation of the same original text as the *Anavatapta Dragon King Sūtra*. Both sūtras claim to have been produced by Zhu Fahu and are thus classified as duplicate translations. According to Sengyou’s catalog, however:
Among the works translated by Zhu Fahu, there is only the *Anavatapta-sūtra* in two fascicles;
the sub-note states that it is also titled the *Sūtra on the Extensive Manifestation of the Propagation of the Way through Samādhi*.
In Sengyou’s *Chusanzang jiji*, among the translations attributed to Zhu Fahu, there is the *Sūtra on the Extensive Manifestation of the Propagation of the Way through Samādhi* in two fascicles.
The sub-note states that it is also titled the *Anavatapta-buddhādhyeṣaṇa-sūtra*.
The *Táng nèidiǎnlù* records both sūtras as translated by Master Hù.
Furthermore, this is also the case in the two catalogs of Zhìfáng’s *Nèidiǎn*.
There is also a one-fascicle *Anavatapta-nāgarāja-sūtra* whose translator during the Western Jin dynasty is lost.
Now, comparing these two sūtras,
there is no difference whatsoever in their wording.
However, because titles were established in various ways,
the numerous catalogs differ;
some even record two sutras under a single title.
There were instances where names and titles were used interchangeably;
at that time, no one attained realization,
and the proliferation of errors grew ever deeper.
Now that one has been discarded and the other preserved,
I hope there will be no further errors or omissions;
I shall retain only this single copy.
Incorporated into this single volume:

*The Sūtra on the Merit of Offering Lamps*, one fascicle; also known as the *Sūtra of Lighting Lamps*. Translated by the Tripitaka Master Narendrayaśas of India during the Northern Qi dynasty. The three aforementioned sūtras comprise ten fascicles in this same volume.
*The Aṅgulimālīya Sūtra*, four fascicles; translated by the Tripitaka Master Guṇabhadra of India during the Song dynasty.

Regarding this *Aṅgulimālīya Sūtra*, the *Catalogue of the Great Zhou* states that it is a different translation of the same text as the seven sūtras such as the *Śikṣāsamuccaya* (or *Aṅgulimālīya*) translated by Dharmarakṣa; however, this is an error. One must not hastily equate them as duplicate translations merely because their titles appear similar. According to the *Sui Catalogue*, the *Śikṣāsamuccaya* (or *Aṅgulimālīya*) is extracted from the *Ekottarika Āgama*, while the six sūtras including the *Aṅgulimālīya* and *Upāli* are excerpted from the *Mahāsaṃnipāta Sūtra*. Since they are neither the same text nor different translations, they remain classified according to the old system as independent works (*dānběn*).
*The Bodhisattva Sūtra*, four fascicles; translated by the Tripitaka Master Jñānagupta and others of India during the Sui dynasty.

From the *Chūn-tien-lu* (Catalogue of Inner and Outer Scriptures): *Mingdu wushi jiaojì jīng* (The Sutra on the Fifty Calculations of the Perfection of Wisdom), two fascicles; alternatively, it may lack the characters "Mingdu" or the "fifty" characters.
Translated by the Anxi Tripiṭaka Master An Shigao of the Later Han. These three aforementioned scriptures, totaling ten fascicles, are contained in the same volume.

*Zhongyin jing* (Sūtra on the Intermediate State), two fascicles; translated by the Śramaṇa Zhu Fonian of Liangzhou during the Yao Qin dynasty. *Dafagujing* (The Great Dharma Drum Sūtra), two fascicles; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Guṇabhadra of India during the Song dynasty. *Wenshushili wenjing* (Sūtra of Mañjuśrī’s Questions), also simply called *Wenwu wenjing*, two fascicles; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Saṃghavarman of Funan during the Liang dynasty. *Yue Shangnü jing* (Sūtra of the Girl Candrottarā), two fascicles; [the daughter of Vimalakīrti]; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Jñānagupta et al. of India during the Sui dynasty. *Dafangguang rulai mizang jing* (The Great Vaipulya Sūtra of the Tathāgata’s Secret Treasury), two fascicles; translator lost. Now appended to the Qin records. These five sūtras, totaling ten fascicles, are contained in the same volume. Regarding the *Dafangguang rulai mizang jing*, the Great Zhou catalog states it is a different translation of the same text as the *Dafangdeng rulai zang jing*. However, upon examining the phrasing and the essential meaning, they differ significantly; therefore, it is treated here as a separate work.

*Mahāyāna-Ghanavyūha-sūtra*, three fascicles; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śīlabhadra of Central India during the Great Tang Dynasty, as recorded in the *Dazhou Catalogue*. *Ghanavyūha-sūtra*, three fascicles; newly translated by the Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of Daxingshan Monastery by imperial decree during the Great Zhou Dynasty. The above two sūtras are the same text with different translations, according to the *Zhenyuan New Catalogue*.

The *Zhan cha shan e ye bao jing* (Sūtra on Divining the Retribution of Good and Evil Karma), two fascicles; also titled the *Dacheng shimu yi jing* (Sūtra on the True Meaning of the Mahāyāna), said to have been extracted from the *Liugen ju jing* (Sūtra on the Collection of the Six Faculties). Translated by the foreign śramaṇa Bodhiruci; its date of translation is unknown, though it appears in the *Dazhou lu* (Catalogue of the Dazhou Era) and is now appended to the *Sui lu* (Catalogue of the Sui Dynasty). The *Lianhuamian jing* (Sūtra of the Lotus Face), two fascicles. Translated by the Tripitaka Master Narendrayaśas of India during the Sui dynasty. These four sūtras, totaling ten fascicles, are contained in the same volume.
The Mañjuśrī-paripṛcchā-bodhisattva-caryā-sūtra, one fascicle;
also known as the Paripṛcchā-sūtra.
Translated by the Yuezhi Tripiṭaka Master Lokakṣema of the Later Han dynasty.

The *Shiyi* (Supplementary Collection) includes the two-fascicle or one-fascicle *Mahāyāna-sūtra on the Merit of Casting Images*, translated during the era of Empress Wu of the Great Tang by the Tripiṭaka Master Ti-yun-po-ye of Khotan.

Regarding the entry for the *Mahāyāna-sūtra on the Merit of Casting Images* in the *Dazhou Lu* (Great Zhou Catalogue), it states that this is a different translation of the same text as the *Sūtra on the Merit of Establishing Images*; however, this is an error, as the wording and meaning differ significantly, and thus it is a separate translation. Also included is the three-fascicle *Vast and Precious Gabled Pavilion Secret Dharani of Good Abiding*.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Bodhiruci of South India during the Great Tang Dynasty;

newly compiled and entered into the canon. *The Sūtra of the Vast and Extensive Pavilion of the Great Jewel*, in three fascicles. The title within the sūtra reads: *The Sūtra of the Secret Dhāraṇī of the Well-Abiding Vast and Extensive Pavilion of the Great Jewel*.
Translated by the Tripitaka Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of Daxingshan Temple, by imperial decree.
The four scriptures and nine fascicles listed at the beginning of the *Zhenyuan New Catalogue* are bound together in one volume.
The *Ekākṣara-uṣṇīṣa-cakravartin-sūtra* in five fascicles— also known as the *Pañca-buddhoṣṇīṣa-sūtra* or in four fascicles—
was translated by the Tripitaka Master Bodhiruci of South India during the Great Tang.

*Newly Compiled Entry: One Scroll of the Yoga Sūtra of the One-Syllable Uṣṇīṣa-Cakra-Rāja*. The title within the sūtra reads: *The Ritual Manual for the Mantra-Ādhāna of the Yoga-Kiṃśara-Uṣṇīṣa-Cakra-Rāja*.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master and Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of Daixingshan Temple by Imperial Decree.
*Zhenyuan New Catalog of the Buddhist Canon*: One Scroll of the Recitation Ritual of the One-Syllable Uṣṇīṣa-Cakra-Rāja.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa of Daxingshan Monastery, the Great Widely Wise Amoghavajra, by Imperial Decree.
*The Brief Recitation Method of the Golden Wheel King Buddha-Uṣṇīṣa*, one fascicle.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa of Daxingshan Monastery, the Great Widely Wise Amoghavajra, by Imperial Decree. The Newly Compiled Catalogue of the Zhenyuan Era.
One fascicle of the *Dharani of the Single-Syllable Heart-Mantra for the Age of Dharma*, newly entered into the catalog during the Zhenyuan era;
translated by the Tripitaka Master Prajñādeva from North India during the Great Tang.
These five new scriptures, totaling nine fascicles, are compiled together in this single volume.

The *Śūraṅgama Sūtra* (The Great Buddha-Uṣṇīṣa Tathāgata’s Secret Cause for Cultivation and Realization, the Definitive Meaning of the Myriad Practices of All Bodhisattvas), ten fascicles, one volume;
translated by the Tripitaka Master Prajñāmitra from Central India during the Great Tang Dynasty at Guangzhou, newly entered into the canon.
The *Mahāvairocana Sūtra* (The Scripture on the Enlightenment and Supernatural Transformations of Mahāvairocana), seven fascicles.
*The Method for Cultivating the Samādhi of Vairocana according to the Yoga of the Vajraśekhara Sūtra*, newly compiled and included in the canon;
translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śubhakarasiṃha of Central India together with the śramaṇa Yi Xing during the Great Tang Dynasty;
and [the version] translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Vajrabodhi, a śramaṇa from South India.
*The Brief Exposition of the Seven-Limb Recitation and Practice according to the *Mahāvairocana-abhisaṃbodhi-tantra*, one fascicle.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master and Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of Daxingshan Temple by Imperial Decree. Recorded in the New Catalogue of the Zhenyuan Era.

*The Brief Compendium of the Recitation and Practice of the *Mahāvairocana-sūtra*, one fascicle; also known as the *Essential Practice of the Brief Five-Limb Recitation*. Recorded in the New Catalogue of the Zhenyuan Era.*
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa of Daxingshan Monastery, the Great One of Vast Wisdom, Amoghavajra, by Imperial Decree.

*The New Catalogue of the Zhenyuan Era*: *The Mantra of the Great Consecration Light of Vairocana Buddha from the Amoghapāśa*, one fascicle; excerpted from the *Amoghapāśa Sūtra*, twenty-eighth [fascicle].
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa of Daxingshan Monastery, the Great One of Vast Wisdom, Amoghavajra, by Imperial Decree.
The *Zhenyuan xinyi mulu* (New Catalogue of Translations of the Zhenyuan Era), Volume One:
The Five Classics in eleven fascicles, bound together in one bundle. 1. *Sūbhahuti-kumāra-sūtra*, three fascicles—also known as the *Sūbhahuti-vinaya*—or two fascicles.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Śubhakarasiṃha of India during the Great Tang; newly included in this catalogue. 2. *Susiddhikara-sūtra*, three fascicles.
The Sūtra of the Mūlamandala-dhāraṇī, newly compiled and included in the catalog;
translated by the Tripitaka Master Śubhakarasiṃha of Central India during the Great Tang Dynasty;
one fascicle (sometimes the word "sūtra" is omitted).
*The Sūtra of the Greatly Powerful King Ucchuṣma*, two fascicles (or three fascicles),
translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Amoghavajra of Daxingshan Temple under imperial decree; the translator is lost and it is now appended to the Liang Record.

*One fascicle of the Essential Gate of the Spiritual Efficacy of the Great Fulfillment Dhāraṇī and Magical Arts Spoken by Vajra-Kṛtyāpāda*, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Anabhibhū of Northern India;
included in the *Zhenyuan New Catalog*.
*One fascicle of the Hundredfold Transformations of the Prohibitive Rites of Vajra-Kṛtyāpāda*, included in the *Zhenyuan New Catalog*.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master and Śramaṇa Anābhibhū of Northern India.
Volume One of the Upper Section of the Newly Recorded Catalogue of the Zhenyuan Era contains six scriptures totaling eleven fascicles in this single bundle.
*The Ritual Manual of Mahātejorucira Ucchuṣma*, one fascicle.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa of Daxingshan Monastery, the Great Widely Wise Amoghavajra, by Imperial Decree.
The New Catalogue of the Zhenyuan Era: *The Ritual Manual for the Accomplishment of the Bodhisattva Āryakrodhavajrakumāra* in three fascicles.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa of Daxingshan Monastery, the Great Widely Wise Amoghavajra, by Imperial Decree.

The *Zhenyuan xinyi dmulu* (New Catalogue of the Zhenyuan Era) lists the *Jingangding yujia zhong lüchchu niansongfa* (The Ritual for Recitation Briefly Extracted from the Yoga of the Vajraśekhara) in four fascicles, also known as the *Jingangding yujia zhenshi da jiaowang jing* (The Great King of Teachings of the True Yoga of the Vajraśekhara) in three fascicles, translated by the Tripitaka Master Vajrabodhi of South India during the Tang dynasty and newly included in the catalogue.
The internal title of the scripture reads: *Jingangding yiqie rulai shizheng da jiaowang jing* (The Great King of Teachings Realized by All Tathāgatas of the Vajraśekhara).
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of Daxingshan Temple by Imperial Decree.
The Upper Volume of the Newly Compiled Catalogue of the Zhenyuan Era contains four sūtras totaling eleven fascicles in this single bundle. These include:

*The Dharma-gate of the Distinctive Holy Ranks of the Thirty-seven Honored Ones of Vajraśekhara Yoga* (one fascicle, including preface). Within the sūtra it is stated: "The Dharma-gate of Cultivation and Realization," followed by the preface.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa of Daxingshan Monastery, the Great Widely Wise Amoghavajra, by Imperial Decree.

*New Catalogue of the Zhenyuan Era*, Volume One: The Scripture on the Thirty-Seven Honored Ones of Vajrayoga. The title within the scripture reads: *The Ritual Text for Prostration and Repentance of the Samādhi of the Supreme Vehicle of the Buddha, the Alternative Name for the Dharmakāya and the Retinue of Internally Realized Wisdom of Vairocana Tathāgata in the Great Maṇḍala of the Vajradhātu*.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master of Daxingshan Monastery, the Great Widely Wise Amoghavajra, by Imperial Decree.

*The Ritual Manual for the Practice of the Five Secrets of Vajraśekhara Yoga*, one fascicle; *The Ritual for the Recitation of Mahāsukha-Vajrasattva, Extracted from the Vajraśekhara-sūtra of the Supreme First Yoga*, one fascicle.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master and Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of Daxingshan Monastery by Imperial Decree.
*The Method for the Recitation of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva from the Vajraśekhara-sūtra of the Supreme First Yoga*, one fascicle. [All listed in] the Newly Entered Catalogue of the Zhenyuan Era.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master of Daxingshan Monastery, the Great Sage Amoghavajra, by Imperial Decree.
*The New Catalogue of the Zhenyuan Era*: One fascicle of the *Vajraśekhara Yoga Homa Rite*. The scripture states:
"Ritual Manual, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master of Daxingshan Monastery, the Great Sage Amoghavajra, by Imperial Decree."

*Jingangding yujia shiba hui zhigui* (The Guide to the Eighteen Assemblies of the Vajraśekhara Yoga), one fascicle. The eighteen characters [indicating the assemblies] are omitted within the scripture itself.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master and Śramaṇa Da Guangzhi Bukong of Daxingshan Monastery by imperial decree.

*Puxian jingang saduo niansong fa* (The Method for Reciting the Mantras of Samantabhadra-Vajrasattva), one fascicle. Listed in the *Zhenyuan xinyu mulu* (New Catalogue of Works Entered during the Zhenyuan Era).
The scripture states: *The Ritual Manual for Yoga Recitation*, translated by the śramaṇa Amoghavajra of Daxingshan Temple by imperial decree during the Zhenyuan era;
one fascicle of the *Ritual Manual for the Practice and Accomplishment of Mahāsukha-vajrasattva*, extracted from the *Śrī-paramādya-tantra-rāja-yoga-sūtra*.
Translated by the Tripitaka Śramaṇa of Daxingshan Monastery, Amoghavajra of Great Universal Wisdom, by Imperial Decree.

*The New Catalogue of the Zhenyuan Era*: *The Great Ritual Manual of Vajraśekhara Trailokyavijaya*, one fascicle. The title within the scripture reads: *The Chapter on the Lotus Great Maṇḍala of All Tathāgatas from the Dharma of the Great Ritual Manual of Vajraśekhara Trailokyavijaya: The Heart Mantra of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva*.
Translated by the Tripitaka Śramaṇa of Daxingshan Monastery, Amoghavajra of Great Universal Wisdom, by Imperial Decree.
*The Extremely Profound and Secret Gate of the Accomplishment of Trailokyavijaya Yoga of the Vajraśekhara*, one fascicle;
translated by the Tripitaka Master and Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of Daxingshan Temple by imperial decree.
*The Scripture on the Radiant Empowerment of Vajrapāṇi*, one fascicle; the Chapter on the Ritual Procedures for Recitation of the Supreme King, the Holy Acala, the Greatly Majestic Wrathful King.
Translated by the Tripitaka Śramaṇa of Daxingshan Monastery, the Great Widely Wise Amoghavajra, by Imperial Decree.
The *Catalogue of New Additions from the Zhenyuan Era*, Volume One: Thirteen scriptures in thirteen fascicles, contained in one bundle; one fascicle is missing, though there are no others lacking.
*The Scripture on the Divine Spells Spoken by the Seven Buddhas*, four fascicles (alternatively titled *The Scripture on the [Spells] Spoken by No One*);
translated during the Jin dynasty, the name of the Tripiṭaka Master is lost; now appended to the catalogue of the Eastern Jin.

Regarding the aforementioned *Scripture on the Divine Spells of the Seven Buddhas*, the Great Zhou Catalogue classifies it as a re-translation, stating that it is the same text as the single-fascicle *Scripture on the Divine Spells of the Seven Buddhas* translated by the foreign Upāsaka Zhi Qian of the Wu dynasty. However, since the text of the single-fascicle version is incomplete and its fascicle count differs, they cannot be directly correlated. Therefore, it is here included within the single-fascicle section according to the old catalogues. *The Scripture on the Great Auspicious Meaning Divine Spells*, two fascicles (alternatively four fascicles).
The *Mañjuśrī-ratnakara-dhāraṇī-sūtra*, one fascicle, translated by the Śramaṇa Shi Tanyao,
the Director of the Shaoguan Bureau during the Northern Wei Dynasty; and the [same] work,
translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Bodhiruci of South India during the Great Tang Dynasty.
*The Sūtra of the Vajra-Flame Dhāraṇī for Stopping Wind and Rain*, one fascicle;
translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Bodhiruci of South India during the Great Tang Dynasty.
Newly included in the canon. *The Āṭavaka Mahāyakṣasenāpati Buddha-Dhāraṇī Sūtra*, one fascicle. Newly included in the canon.
*The Dhāraṇī Sūtra of King Amitābha’s Drum-Sound*,
one fascicle; translated by an unknown hand, included in the *Shiyi* (Supplement) and now appended to the Jin Record.
One fascicle of the *Mahāsamantabhadra-dhāraṇī-sūtra*, translated by an unknown hand, included in the *Shiyi* (Supplement) and now appended to the Liang Record.
*The Sutra of the Great Seven Jewels Dhāraṇī*, one fascicle; translated by an unknown hand, included in the *Shiyi* (Supplemental Collection) and now appended to the Liang Record.
One fascicle of the *Ṣaḍakṣara-mahādhāraṇī-sūtra*, translated by an unknown hand,
included in the *Shiyi* (Supplement) and now appended to the Liang Record.

The *Anzhai shenzhou jing* (Sutra of the Spirit-Mantra for Dwelling Peacefully), one fascicle; its translator lost, included among the "Supplements to Lost Translations" and now appended to the Liang Record.

*Manirodhan Sūtra*, one fascicle; translated by the Śramaṇa Zhu Tanwulan of the Western Regions during the Eastern Jin dynasty; its provenance was lost during the Later Han, and it was subsequently included in the *Shiyi*.
*Sengqieshi Bata Suoshuo Shenzhou Jing* (The Scripture of Divine Incantations Spoken by the Illusionist Bata), one fascicle; the catalog records that "Illusionist" is a misspelling for "Unspoken."
*The Dhāraṇī Sūtra for Protecting All Children*, translated by the Śramaṇa Zhu Tanwulan of the Western Regions during the Eastern Jin dynasty; one fascicle.
*The Dhāraṇī Sūtra of the Heart of All Buddhas*, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Bodhiruci of India during the Northern Wei dynasty; one fascicle.
The Scripture of the Dhāraṇī for Deliverance from Suffering and Calamity, translated by the Tripitaka Master Xuanzang of the Great Tang, one fascicle;
translated by the Tripitaka Master Xuanzang of the Great Tang.

The *Pumimi Dharani Sutra*, one fascicle, translated by the Tripitaka Master Xuanzang of the Great Tang, as recorded in the *Chujing Lu* (Catalogue of Scriptures Issued from the Imperial Library), No. 8;
and the *Shishi Dharani Sutra*, one fascicle, as recorded in the *Chujing Lu*.
Record of the Inner Scriptures Translated by Tripitaka Master Xuanzang of the Great Tang:
*The Dhāraṇī Sūtra of the Six Gates*, one fascicle;
translated by Tripitaka Master Xuanzang of the Great Tang.
*Chūnadianlu qingjing guanshiyin puxian tuoluoni jing*, one fascicle;
translated by the Śramaṇa Shi Zhitong of Zongchi Monastery during the Great Tang.
It is recorded in the *Dazhou lu* as the nineteenth of the upper section, comprising twenty-three fascicles in the same volume.

The *Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva Supreme Vidyārāja Heart Sūtra*, two fascicles; the internal title reads: *The Vast Extensive Ritual Manual of the Vajra Terrifying Assembly: The Sūtra of the Heart-King of the Three Times of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva*, Chapter One: Introduction.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master of Daxingshan Monastery, the Śramaṇa Amoghavajra, by Imperial Decree. Included in the *New Catalogue of the Zhenyuan Era*.

The *Ritual Manual for the Contemplative Practice of the Heart Mantra of the Holy Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva*, one fascicle; the internal title reads: *The Yoga Ritual Manual for Contemplative Practice*.
Translated by the Tripitaka Śramaṇa of Daxingshan Temple, the Great Widely Wise Amoghavajra, by Imperial Decree.

*The Ritual Manual for the Recitation of the Lotus Family Yoga for the Accomplishment of the Great Compassion of Avalokiteśvara*, one fascicle. This scripture is also titled *The Accomplishment of the Great Compassionate Avalokiteśvara*.
Translated by the Tripitaka Śramaṇa of Daxingshan Temple, the Great Widely Wise Amoghavajra, by Imperial Decree.
*The Dhāraṇī Sūtra of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara of the Leaf-Garment*, one fascicle. The dhāraṇī text is omitted within this sūtra.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master and Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of Daxingshan Temple by imperial decree.
*The Ritual for Recitation of the Yoga Lotus Family*, one fascicle. Included in the *New Catalogue of the Zhenyuan Era*.
Translated by the Śramaṇa Mahāprajñā Amoghavajra of Daxingshan Temple by Imperial Decree.
*The Ritual Manual for the Recitation of the Heart of the Lotus Family of the Vajraśekhara*, one fascicle. The title within the scripture reads:
*The Ritual Manual for Recitation*, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śramaṇa Mahāprajñā Amoghavajra of Daxingshan Temple by Imperial Decree.
One fascicle of the *Dhāraṇī Secret Method of the Immovable Messenger*, newly included in the Zhenyuan Catalogue;
translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Vajrabodhi, a Śramaṇa from South India.
One fascicle of the *Tilaka-samaya Sūtra*, newly included in the Zhenyuan Catalogue; the title within the sūtra itself reads: *The Recitation Method of the Immovable Messenger of the Tilaka-samaya*.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of Daxingshan Monastery, by Imperial Decree.
*The New Catalogue of the Zhenyuan Era*: The *Jñānolkā Dhāraṇī Sūtra*, one fascicle;
translated during the reign of the Empress of the Great Tang by the Tripiṭaka Master Divākara of Khotan.
*The Dhāraṇī Sūtra on the Assemblage of All Buddhas*, one fascicle;
translated during the era of Empress Wu of the Great Tang by the Tripiṭaka Master from Khotan, Devendraprajñā. Recorded in the *Dazhou Catalogue*.
*The Divine Mantra Sūtra of the Great Sovereign Dhāraṇī of Immediate Attainment*, one fascicle. Recorded in the *Dazhou Catalogue*.
Translated during the era of Empress Wu of the Great Tang by the Tripiṭaka Master from Northern India, Prajñādeva (Bǎosīwéi).
Recorded in the Catalogue of the Great Zhou. *The Sūtra of the Dhāraṇī of Universal Radiance and Great Peacock Queen* in two fascicles. The title within the sūtra reads:

*The Sūtra of the Dhāraṇī of the Great Peacock Queen, the Sovereign of Great Radiance, the Supreme Wish-Fulfilling Jewel Seal of the Heart, the Unconquerable*, translated by the Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa of Daxingshan Monastery, Amoghavajra (Dàguǎngzhì Bùkōng), by imperial decree.
*Zhengyuan xinru mulu*: *Baiqian yintuoluoni jing*, one fascicle, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda of Khotan during the era of the Great Tang Empress;
newly compiled and entered into the catalog. The fourteen sūtras totaling fifteen fascicles herein are bound in the same volume.
*The Dhāraṇī Sūtra of the Divine Incantation for Saving the Face-Burning Hungry Ghosts*, one fascicle; also known as *The Incantation for Bestowing upon Hungry Ghosts*.

This latter version includes an appended incantation for bestowing water, translated during the reign of Empress Wu of the Great Tang by the Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda of Khotan, and newly included in the canon.
*Sūtra of the Dhāraṇī for Saving the Mouth-Burning Hungry Ghosts*, one fascicle. The title within the sūtra reads: *The Buddha-Spoken Dhāraṇī Sūtra for Delivering the Mouth-Burning Hungry Ghosts*.
The *Ratnarāja-dhāraṇī-mantra-sūtra*, one fascicle, translated during the era of the Empress Dowager of the Great Tang by the Tripiṭaka Master Yijing;
newly entered into the catalog during the Zhenyuan era,
translated by the Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa of Daxingshan Monastery, Da Guangzhi Bukong, by imperial decree.
The Sūtra on the Dhāraṇī Mantra of the Bodhisattva Gandharāja, newly included in the catalog;
translated by the Tripitaka Master Yijing of the Great Tang.
The Sūtra of the King Adorned with All Merits, newly included in the catalog.
The King of Mantras for Eradicating Karmic Obstructions,
Newly Compiled and Included in the Catalogue, translated by the Tripitaka Master Yi Jing of the Great Tang, one fascicle;
translated by the Tripitaka Master Yi Jing of the Great Tang.
*The Sūtra of the Auspicious Night*, one fascicle;
newly included in the catalogue, translated by Tripiṭaka Master Yijing during the era of Empress Wu of the Great Tang.

*The Method for Seeking the Retention of What is Heard through the Most Supreme Heart Dhāraṇī of the Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha, Who Can Fulfill All Wishes*, one fascicle; newly included in the catalogue.
The Chapter on the Accomplishment of All Meanings,
translated by the Tripitaka Master Śubhakarasiṃha of Central India during the Great Tang Dynasty;
newly included in the canon as the *Vajraśekhara Sūtra*, Chapter on the Five-Syllable Heart Dhāraṇī of Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva, one fascicle.

The Ritual for the Recitation of Vajrarāja Bodhisattva, newly compiled and included in the canon, one fascicle. Translated by the Tripitaka Master Vajrabodhi of South India during the Great Tang Dynasty. Within this scripture is the *Guhyamantra-japa-vidhi*.
Translated by the Tripitaka Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of Daxingshan Temple, by imperial decree.

*The Essential Yoga Method of Avalokiteśvara and Cintāmaṇicakra Bodhisattva*, one fascicle; translated by the Tripitaka Master Vajrabodhi of South India during the Great Tang Dynasty; newly included in the catalog.

Regarding the three sutras beginning with *Ākāśagarbha* and the four preceding fascicles of the *Yoga* [tantras], these all derive from the *Vajraśekhara Sūtra*. The Sanskrit original of that scripture consists of one hundred thousand stanzas; these four scriptures are abridged essential extracts and were translated as such, rather than being complete versions.
*The Yoga of the Wish-Fulfilling Wheel of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva*, one fascicle.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of Daxingshan Temple by imperial decree.
*The Method for Reciting the Mantra of the Wish-Fulfilling Wheel*, one fascicle, newly entered into the catalog during the Zhenyuan era.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa Mahāprajñā Amoghavajra of Daxingshan Monastery, by Imperial Decree.
*The Sūtra on the Buddha-Bhūmi*, one fascicle, translated by the Great Tang Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang;

listed in the *Neidian lu* (Inner Canon Catalogue) with its commentary in seven fascicles. *The Sūtra of the Brief Teaching and Admonition Spoken by the Buddha as He Was About to Enter Parinirvāṇa*, one fascicle; also called *The Sūtra of the Buddha’s Imminent Parinirvāṇa*, or alternatively, *The Sūtra of the Bequeathed Teaching*.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kumārajīva of the Yao Qin Dynasty.

There is one fascicle of commentary (*śāstra*). [Note: Regarding this *Śāsanānuśāsanī-sūtra*, it was recorded in ancient catalogs as being mostly contained within the Hīnayāna Vinaya or compiled among the Hīnayāna sūtras. Now, because the commentary translated by Dharma Master Paramārtha explains it largely from the perspective of the Mahāyāna—such that the distinction between Mahāyāna and Hīnayāna is not evident—it has been moved here and compiled with this [text].
*Bodhicittotpādana-sūtra* (One Fascicle), translated by the Indian Tripiṭaka Master Jñānagupta and others of the Sui Dynasty. *Buddhamudrāsamādhi-sūtra* (One Fascicle).
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master An Shigao of Parthia during the Later Han Dynasty;
supplemented and included in the *Mañjuśrī-parinirvāṇa-sūtra*, one fascicle;
translated by the lay devotee Nie Daozhen of the Western Jin Dynasty.
*Pusa benqi jing* (Sutra on the Original Arising of the Bodhisattva), one fascicle;
sometimes without the character "qi" (arising).
Translated by the Western Jin layman Nie Daozhen. Recorded in the *Shiyi*. Alternative title: *Yichu pusa benqi jing*.
*Shiyi bianru qianfo yinyuan jing* (Supplementary Compilation on the Causes and Conditions of the Thousand Buddhas), one fascicle;
translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kumārajīva of the Yaoqin period.
*Faxiang lu*: *Xianshou jing* (Sūtra of the Lady Xianshou), one fascicle; also known as the *Xianshou furen jing*.

*The Sūtra of the Bodhisattva Candraprabha*, one fascicle. Translated by the Śramaṇa Shi Shengjian of the Qifu Qin. Also known as *The Boy Candraprabha* or *The Youth Candraprabha*. Translated by the Upāsaka Zhi Qian of Yuezhi during the Wu dynasty. Note:

This *Sūtra of the Bodhisattva Candraprabha* is listed in the *Dazhou Catalogue* as a re-translation; however, it is an error to claim it is the same text as the *Sūtra of the Youth Candraprabha*, for their wording and meaning differ entirely, and thus it is a single, independent translation. *The Sūtra of the Heart-Illumination*, one fascicle. Also titled *The Sūtra on the Offering of Rice Gruel by the Brahmin Woman Heart-Illumination*.

Translated by the Tripitaka Master Zhu Fahu of the Western Jin. *The Sūtra of the Extinction of Darkness in the Ten Directions*, one fascicle. Also known as *The Sūtra of the Ten Extinctions of Darkness*.
*The Sūtra of the Deer Mother*, one fascicle, translated by the Tripitaka Master Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin.

Translated by the Tripitaka Master Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin. In the aforementioned catalog, there is additionally the *Sūtra of the Deer Child*, one fascicle, which states it was translated during the Wu dynasty by the foreign Upāsaka Zhi Qian; however, its wording is identical to the preceding *Sūtra of the Deer Mother*, differing only in its title. Therefore, it is not recorded here separately.

*Mārapratyarthika-sūtra* (The Scripture on the Subduing of Māra), one fascicle; translated by the Western Jin Tripiṭaka Master Dharmarakṣa. The twenty-six scriptures above comprise twenty-six fascicles in this single volume.

*Rājaputra Śrīprabha-sūtra* (The Scripture of Prince Śrīprabha), one fascicle—also known as the *Rāṣṭrapāla-paripṛcchā Śrīprabha-rāja-sūtra*; translated by the Western Jin Tripiṭaka Master Dharmarakṣa. Regarding the aforementioned *Śrīprabha-rāja-sūtra*, it is recorded in the *Dazhou Catalogue* as a "re-translation. This is an error, as it is claimed to be a different translation of the same text as the *Sulakṣaṇa-sūtra*. However, since the wording and meaning differ, it is included here as a standalone text.
*Mahāyāna-sūtra* (Dàyì jīng), one fascicle;
translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Guṇabhadra of India during the Song dynasty. *Dṛḍhā-dārikā-sūtra* (Jiāngù nǚ jīng), one fascicle; also titled *Sthirā-dārikā-sūtra*;
translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Narendrayaśas of India during the Sui dynasty. *Sārthavāha-devaputra-paripṛcchā-sūtra* (Shāngzhǔ tiānzǐ suowèn jīng), one fascicle; alternatively titled *Wúsuǒwèn*.
*The Sūtra of the Supreme King of All Dharmas*, one fascicle; translated by the Indian Tripiṭaka Master Jñānagupta and others of the Sui dynasty.
*The Sūtra of the Questions of the Bodhisattva Siṃhavikrīḍita-rāja*, one fascicle; also known as the *Sūtra of the Eight Maṇḍalas*;

translated by the Indian Tripiṭaka Master Nadi of the Great Tang dynasty, recorded in the *Dazhou Catalogue*. *The Sūtra of the Discourse on Royal Governance Spoken by the Buddha for King Udayana*, one fascicle.
Translated by the Tripitaka Śramaṇa of Daxingshan Monastery, the Great Widely Wise Amoghavajra, by Imperial Decree.
*The Sūtra on the Questions of Bodhisattva Vimalamati Concerning the Paying of Homage to the Buddha*, one fascicle;
translated by the Tripitaka Master from India, Nadi, during the Tang Dynasty. Newly entered into the catalog of the Zhenyuan era.

Extracted from the *Dazhou lu shiyi* (Supplementary Records of the Dazhou Era) and included here: *The Sutra on the Merit Arising from Receiving and Maintaining the Names of the Seven Buddhas*, one fascicle;
translated by the Tripitaka Master Xuanzang of the Great Tang.

*Chunei dianlu Folin niepan jifa zhu jing* (Record of Buddhist Scriptures: The Sūtra on the Duration of the Dharma Spoken by the Buddha as He Was About to Enter Nirvāṇa), one fascicle; alternatively titled with the character "ban" (parinirvāṇa).
Translated by the Great Tang Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang.
*Fanjing tu Jizhao shenbian sanmei jing* (Diagram of the Scripture Translation: The Sūtra on the Samādhi of Silent Illumination and Divine Transformation), one fascicle.
*The Sūtra on the Prophecy Bestowed upon Cāmarapāti*, one fascicle, translated by the Tripitaka Master Xuanzang of the Great Tang;
*The Sūtra on Neither Increasing nor Decreasing*, one fascicle, translated by the Indian Tripitaka Master Bodhiruci of the Northern Wei.
Some claim that the version in two fascicles is erroneous;
it consists of the *Sūtra on the Merit of Building Stūpas* in one fascicle translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Bodhiruci of Central India during the Northern Wei dynasty,
and the [same] work translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Divākara of Central India during the Great Tang dynasty.
Extracted from the *Dazhou lu shiyi* (Supplementary Records of the Great Zhou), compiled as the one-fascicle *Right-Circumambulation of the Buddha Stūpa Merit Sūtra*,
also known as the *Merit of Circumambulating the Stūpa*.
The Mahāyāna Sūtra on the Four Dharmas, translated during the era of Empress Wu of the Great Tang by the Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda of Khotan;
newly compiled and included in the canon, one fascicle.
Translated during the era of Empress Wu of the Great Tang by the Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda of Khotan.
*The Mahāyāna Sūtra on the Questions of the Virtuous Woman*, one fascicle; newly included in the canon, a third translation identical in text to the *Sūtra of the Indian Woman Shouyi*.
Newly verified and produced during the era of Empress Wu of the Great Tang by the Indian Tripiṭaka Master Bodhiruci.
*The Mahāyāna Sūtra on the Flowing Through All Existences*, one fascicle; recorded in the *Dazhou Lu*.
The Causes and Conditions of King Wonderful Color, newly compiled and included in the canon during the reign of the Empress of the Great Tang, translated by Tripiṭaka Master Yijing. One fascicle.
Translated by Tripiṭaka Master Yijing during the reign of the Empress of the Great Tang.
*The Sūtra on the Seal of the Dharma Spoken by the Buddha for the Nāga King Sāgara*, one fascicle;
translated by the Tripitaka Master Yijing of the Great Tang.
Newly included in the catalog. *The Sūtra on King Siṃhasauḍasa’s Abandonment of Harm*, one fascicle. Newly included in the catalog.
*The Sūtra on the Offering of the *Gwan-lak* (Ancestral Feast) after the Parinirvāṇa*, translated by the Śramaṇa Shi Zhiyan of Zhixiang Monastery during the Great Tang Dynasty;
newly included in the canon. One fascicle. Also titled *The Sūtra on the *Gwan-lak* for the Four Classes of Disciples*, or simply *The Sūtra on the *Gwan-lak***.

Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin Dynasty. Note: Regarding this *Gwan-lak Sūtra*, the *Dazhou Catalogue* and other records state that it is a retranslation and that it is the same text as the *Ullambana Sūtra* but with a different translation. This is an error. Now, having examined the text, as the wording differs, it is treated here as a separate work.

*The Scripture on the Names of the Eight Classes of Beings*, one fascicle; also known as *The Scripture on Entering the Buddha*. Translated by the Bactrian Brahmin Gautama Prajñāruci during the Northern Wei dynasty. The twenty-two scriptures comprising twenty-three fascicles above are contained in the same volume.

Regarding the *Buddhanāma-aṣṭakula-sūtra*, the *Dazhou lu* states that it is a different translation of the same text as the *Aṣṭamaṅgalaka-sūtra*; however, this is an error. Although the number eight is the same, the locations where they were preached differ entirely and their purposes are distinct; therefore, it is treated as a separate text.

*The Bodhisattva’s Internal Practice of the Six Pāramitās Sūtra*, one fascicle; alternatively titled *The Sūtra of the Six Pāramitās*. Master Dao’an states it was produced from the Vaipulya section. Translated by the śramaṇa Yan Fotiao of Linhuai during the Later Han dynasty. Included in the *Shiyi* (Supplementary Collection) as part of the *Mahāyāna-ratnaguṇasaṃcayagāthā Sūtra*, ten fascicles. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Prajñā, a śramaṇa of Kapiśa who was conferred the purple robe, by imperial decree. *The Mahāpuṣpa-sūtra on the Elder Asking the Buddha about the Nārāyaṇa Power*, one fascicle. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Prajñā, a śramaṇa of Kapiśa who was conferred the purple robe. The above three sūtras, totaling twelve fascicles, are contained in the same volume according to the *Zhenyuan New Catalogue*.
*Mahāyāna-mūla-jātaka-citta-bhūmi-parīkṣā-sūtra*, eight fascicles;
translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Prajñā of Kapiśa during the Great Tang Dynasty. From the time of the Wei capital (Luoyang) onwards, it has been included within the *Zhenyuan lu*.
This collection consists of one fascicle: the *Bodhisattva-tiṣṭhati-kṣudra-vyāghrī-caitya-nidāna-sūtra*. Sengyou’s catalogue refers to this as the *Śarīra-pradāna-kṣudra-vyāghrī-sūtra*.

Postscript to the Translation of the *Vajrasamādhi-svabhāva-viśuddhy-avināśy-aniruddha-sūtra* (One Scroll), also titled the *Vajra-viśuddhi-sūtra*, translated by the Śramaṇa Shi Fasheng of Gaochang during the Northern Liang Dynasty;
newly identified as a work of lost translation.

Attached to the *Sanchin lu* (Records of the Three Qin): one fascicle of the *Sīmanamukha-buddha-pūrvabhava-sūtra*, newly classified as a lost translation and attached to the *Sanchin lu*. Regarding the *Vajra-viśuddhi-sūtra*, various catalogs state it was translated during the Wu dynasty by the foreign Upāsaka Zhi Qian; however, its name also appears among the lost translations of the Later Han. Furthermore, regarding the *Sīmanamukha-buddha-sūtra*, various catalogs state it was translated by the Tripitaka Master Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin. Now, upon close examination, the phrasing and sentences of these two sūtras do not correspond to those translated by Qian or Dharmarakṣa; they appear rather to have been translated by Kumārajīva and others from the Qin or Liang periods onward.

*The Sūtra on the Wife of the Elder Dharmamati*, one fascicle. Translator unknown. It is listed in An Shigao’s *Catalogue of Heterodox Scriptures from the Liang Territory*; it is now also appended to the Liang catalogue. *The Sūtra of the Kingdom of Sāla*, one fascicle; alternatively titled *The Sūtra of the King of Sāla*. Translator unknown. It is now appended to the Eastern Jin catalogue. Regarding these two sūtras, the *Fashang Catalogue* states that both were translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kumārajīva of the Yao Qin dynasty. However, upon careful examination, the phrasing and style of both texts do not match those translated by Master Kumārajīva. They appear to belong to the Jin or Wei periods. As for the *Sūtra on the Wife of the Elder Dharmamati*, it was previously listed in An Gong’s *Catalogue of Heterodox Scriptures from the Liang Territory*; it is now also appended to the Liang catalogue. The *Sūtra of the Kingdom of Sāla* is appended to the Jin catalogue.
The Sūtra of the Ten Auspiciousnesses, one fascicle;
translator lost, now appended to the Qin Records. The Sūtra of the Twelve Names of the Goddess Śrī.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa Mahāprajñā Amoghavajra of Daxingshan Temple by Imperial Decree.

*New Catalogue of the Zhenyuan Era*, Volume One: The Sūtra of the Great Auspicious Goddess. The title within the sūtra reads: *The Buddha-Spoken Mahāyāna Sūtra of the Twelve Mudrās and One Hundred and Eight Names of the Great Auspicious Goddess, the Stainless*.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa Mahāprajñā Amoghavajra of Daxingshan Temple by Imperial Decree.
*The Scripture on the Meaning of the Elder’s Daughter Ātreyī and the Lion*, one fascicle; translated by an unknown hand,
now appended to the Liang dynasty catalog from the *Zhenyuan New Catalog*.

The *Shiyi bianru yiqiezhi guangming xianren cixin yinyuan bushirou jing* (Supplementary Collection: The Sūtra on the Causes and Conditions of the Compassionate Heart of the Immortal Sarvajñāprabha Who Does Not Eat Meat), one fascicle;
