These were transcribed by Wenxuan.

The above forty-three sections comprising two hundred and ninety-eight fascicles from the Avataṃsaka Sūtra were collated against various catalogs and found to have been transcribed by Xiao Ziliang, Prince Wenxuan of Jingling and Minister of State under the Southern Qi dynasty. The Changfang Record states: [as follows].
The King was fond of extensive research;

he personally compiled and edited this work as a memorandum modeled after the *Lishi* (Calendar). He did not expect it to be transmitted to later generations, yet scholars followed one after another in copying and reading it.
Consequently, people of the world interpolated various elements, confusing and corrupting the original text.
Therefore, I have set forth the fundamental framework so that one may understand the details through them.

However, those works titled with the character "抄" (extracted/abridged) are all of its various sub-categories; if one carefully examines their beginnings and ends, they will be distinguished on their own.
As the *Neidian lu* states:
Since this differs from the original title of the scripture, it is recorded separately here so that future readers may know its origin.

Nevertheless, its literary flavor is pervasive and its principles are satisfying; it serves as a bridge for the vast and manifold learning of the common people and accommodates the diverse paths of those with spiritual inclinations—thus, a Way indeed exists herein.
The meaning is neither doubtful nor erroneous;
yet, in the catalogs of Sengyou, Huichang, Fang, and others, all have annotated these as "doubtful scriptures.
This was because they feared that [the texts] might involve the lingering waves of decadence and thus lose their original essence.

*Jìngdù sānmèi chāo* (Excerpts on the Samādhi of Pure Deliverance), one fascicle; *Lǜjīng záchāo* (Miscellaneous Excerpts on the Vinaya Sūtras), one fascicle; *Běnqǐ chāo* (Excerpts on the Original Arising), one fascicle. Yòu states that these were recorded in the old catalog as *Shàn chāojīng* (Excerpted Sūtra of Śyāma), one fascicle; *Wǔbǎi fànlǜ jīng chāo* (Excerpts from the Five Hundred Brahmanical Vinaya Sūtras), one fascicle; and *Dàhǎi shēnqiǎn chāojīng* (Excerpted Sūtra on the Deep Perilousness of the Great Ocean), one fascicle. Yòu states that these six aforementioned sūtras are all old excerpts.
Regarding the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra* in one hundred and eighty-nine fascicles, Sengyou states:
"This single scripture was compiled in recent times by collecting and arranging various sūtras according to their categories.

Although it is titled the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra*, it is included among the miscellaneous extracts. It follows the sixty-four sections and five hundred and one fascicles from the six meanings of the Buddha-dharma downward."
Furthermore, their titles are conflated with those of the authentic scriptures;
their wording has been increased or decreased, or new texts have been mixed in with different meanings under newly established titles.
If these were collected alongside the orthodox canon, there would be a danger that the "jade" and the "stone" would become indistinguishably intermingled.
If one were to categorize this as a forgery while simultaneously inferring that it has a reliable source,
it would be truly difficult to determine its status between these two alternatives.
For now, I shall include it among the forgeries at the end of the old records.
May future students, in their investigations and readings, take the trouble to examine in detail both its merits and its shortcomings.

included in the New Catalogue of the Zhenyuan Era. Two sheets. translated by the Tripiṭaka Master of Daxingshan Monastery, the Śramaṇa Amoghavajra, by Imperial Decree. *The Scripture on the Gate of Entering the Seal through the Power of Faith*, five fascicles. (3 sheets) [Included in] the *New Catalogue of the Zhenyuan Era*.

*The Great Vaipulya Scripture on the Inconceivable Realm of the Tathāgata*, one fascicle.

*The Sūtra on the Buddha-Ground*, one fascicle.

*Sahasrabuddha-nidāna-sūtra*, one fascicle, eleven sheets.

*The Scripture on the Extinction of Darkness in the Ten Directions*, three sheets; also known as *The Scripture on the Extinction of Darkness in the Ten Directions*, six sheets.

*The Sūtra of the Great Meaning* (one fascicle).
*The Sūtra of the Firm Woman*, one fascicle; also known as *The Sūtra of the Resolute Woman*, six pages.

*The Scripture on the Treatise on Royal Law and Governance Spoken by the Buddha for King Udayana*, one fascicle; nine folios.

Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master of Daixingshan Monastery, the Śramaṇa Amoghavajra, by Imperial Decree. *The Scripture on the Dharma of Paying Homage to the Buddha as Asked by the Bodhisativisimalaprajñā*, one fascicle.

*The Sūtra on the Merit of Building Stūpas*, one volume, seven sheets.

*The Mahāyāna Sūtra of the Questions of the Virtuous Woman*, one fascicle.

*Buddha-deśita-sāgara-nāgarāja-dharma-paryāya-sūtra*, one fascicle.
One fascicle, four pages: *The Sūtra on King Siṃhasauḍasa’s Prohibition of Meat*. One fascicle, two pages:

*The Sūtra on the Wax-Casting Ceremony after the Parinirvāṇa*, also known as *The Sūtra on the Wax-Casting Ceremony for the Four Classes of Followers after the Parinirvāṇa*, or simply *The Sūtra on the Wax-Casting Ceremony*.
One fascicle: *The Sūtra of the Names of the Buddhas of the Eight Classes*.

*Pusa nei xi liu boluomi jing* (The Sutra on the Bodhisattva’s Internal Practice of the Six Pāramitās), one fascicle; also called *Nei liu boluomi jing*. Three sheets. *Dacheng liqu liu boluomiduo jing* (The Mahāyāna Sūtra on the Principles and Sequence of the Six Pāramitās), ten fascicles. Newly entered into the Zhenyuan Catalogue. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Prajña of Kaśmīra by imperial decree. *Dahua yan changzhe wen fo naluo yenli jing* (The Sūtra of the Great Flower Adornment Asked by the Elder on the Nārāyaṇa Power of the Buddha), one fascicle. Newly entered into the Zhenyuan Catalogue. One sheet. Imperial Preface. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Prajña of Kaśmīra by imperial decree. *Bore boluomiduo xin jing* (The Heart Sūtra of the Perfection of Wisdom), one fascicle. Newly entered into the Zhenyuan Catalogue. One sheet. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Prajña of Kaśmīra. These four sūtras, totaling thirteen fascicles, are contained in the same volume.

The *Bodhicittotpāda-sūtra* (Jātaka-bhūmi-citta-parīkṣā-sūtra), eight fascicles, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śramaṇa Prajña of Kapiśī during the Great Tang Dynasty, and included by imperial decree in the Zhenyuan Catalogue. This aforementioned scripture consists of eight fascicles in one volume.

*The Sūtra on the Causes and Conditions of the Bodhisattva Throwing Himself to a Starving Tiger and the Subsequent Erection of a Stūpa*, one fascicle; the *Monk You Record* states it consists of twelve sheets of paper and is titled *The Sūtra on Giving One’s Body to a Starving Tiger*.
*The Sūtra on the Innate Purity of the Vajrasamādhi, Which is Unbreakable and Undestructible*, one fascicle; also known as the *Vajra-purity Sūtra*, eight sheets of paper.
*The Sūtra on the Previous Life of the Buddha Siṃhacandra*, one fascicle.
*The Scripture on the Wife of the Elder Dharmavatsa*, one fascicle, three sheets;
*The Scripture on the Kingdom of Sala* (also known as *The Scripture on the King of Sala*), one fascicle, four sheets;
*The Scripture on the Ten Auspiciousnesses*, one fascicle.
*The Scripture on the Twelve Names of the Auspicious Goddess Vasudhārā*, one fascicle; listed in the *Zhenyuan New Catalogue*, two pages.

Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master of Daxingshan Monastery, the Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of Great Wisdom, by imperial decree. *The Scripture of the Great Auspicious Goddess*, one fascicle; the internal title reads *The Buddha-Spoken Mahāyāna Scripture of the Stainless One Hundred and Eight Names in Twelve Sections of the Great Auspicious Goddess*.

Listed in the *Zhenyuan New Catalogue*, six pages. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master of Daxingshan Monastery, the Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of Great Wisdom, by imperial decree. *The Scripture on the Lion’s Roar of the Definitive Meaning by the Elder’s Daughter Ātīcā*, one fascicle.
*The Sūtra on the Causes and Conditions of the Compassionate Heart of the Immortal Sarvajñāprabha: On Not Eating Meat*, five sheets;
one scroll. *The Vajrasamādhi Sūtra*, two scrolls, or one scroll, twenty-seven sheets.
*The Sūtra on the Extinction of the Dharma*, one scroll.
*The Sutra on the Profound and Great Dedication*, three fascicles; one volume.
*The Sutra of the Prince of the Heavenly King Piluo*, four fascicles; also called *The Sutra of Prince Piluo*, or omitting the words "Heavenly King.
*The Sutra on the Dharma-gate of Pure Conduct for Upāsikās*, two fascicles; also simply called *The Sutra of Pure Conduct*, or omitting the word "Sutra."
*The Sutra on the Eight Great Realizations of the Noble Persons*, one fascicle, thirty-two pages;
*The Sutra of the Three Grades of Disciples*, one fascicle, three pages—also called *The Sutra on the Awakening of the Three Grades of Disciples*;
*The Sutra of the Four Classes*, one fascicle—also called *The Sutra of the Four Classes of Disciples* or *The Sutra of the Learning of the Four Classes*.
*The Sutra on Future Transformations*, three sheets; also called *The Sutra on the Consciousness of Future Transformations*, two sheets.
*The Sutra on the Almsround of Past Buddhas*, one scroll; also called *The Sutra on Past Ages*, two sheets.
*The Sutra on the Twelve Dhūtas*, one scroll; also known as *The Head of the Śramaṇa*.
One fascicle of the *Cūḍāpanthaka-sūtra*, three pages;
one fascicle of the *Dīrghāyu-rāja-sūtra*, six pages;
and one fascicle of the *Dharmasthititā-sūtra*.
Two scrolls: twenty-four sūtras in twenty-four fascicles, bound together in one volume. Mahāyāna Vinaya: twenty-seven sections in fifty-five fascicles, in five volumes.

*Bodhisattvabhūmi-vidhāraṇa-sūtra* (or *Bodhisattva-bhūmi-śīla-sūtra*, also called *Bodhisattva-bhūmi-śāstra* or simply *Bodhisattva-bhūmi-sūtra*): ten fascicles—or eight fascicles—bound together in one volume; 186 sheets. *Bodhisattva-śīla-saṃvara-sūtra*: nine fascicles (also known as *Bodhisattva-bhūmi*), or ten fascicles; 180 sheets. *Śuddha-karmāvaraṇa-viśodhana-sūtra*: one fascicle; 15 sheets. The above two sūtras, ten fascicles in total, are bound together in one volume.

The *Upāsaka-śīla-sūtra* (The Sutra on the Precepts for Lay Disciples), in seven fascicles, or five, or six, or ten; this is the precept for the lay bodhisattva. One hundred thirty-one pages. The *Brahmajāla-sūtra* (The Brahma’s Net Sutra), in two fascicles. Thirty-six pages. The *Sūtra on Receiving the Ten Good Precepts*, in one fascicle. Sixteen pages. The *Ritual for Receiving the Bodhicitta Precepts*, in one fascicle. The title within the text reads: *Text for Repentance upon Receiving Precepts according to the Teaching of the Supreme Vehicle, Compiled by the Ācārya of Samantabhadra-yoga*. Included in the *Zhenyuan New Catalogue*. Three pages. Translated by the Tripitaka Master of Daxingshan Monastery, the Śramaṇa of Great Vast Wisdom, Amoghavajra, by imperial decree. The above four sutras, totaling eleven fascicles, are contained in the same volume.

*The Sūtra on the Original Action of the Bodhisattva’s Diadem-Ornament*, two fascicles, thirty-nine sheets. *The Buddha-Treasury Sūtra*, four fascicles—also titled *The Sūtra of Selecting All Dharmas*—alternatively in three or two fascicles, seventy sheets. *Bodhisattva Precept Text*, one fascicle, translated by Dharmakṣema, eleven sheets. *Bodhisattva Precept Text*, one fascicle, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang, eighteen sheets. *Bodhisattva Precept Karma Text*, one fascicle, six sheets. *Bodhisattva Good Precepts Sūtra*, one fascicle, including the *Upāli’s Questions on the Method for Receiving the Bodhisattva Precepts*, fifteen sheets. The above six sūtras, totaling ten fascicles, are contained in the same volume.
*The Bodhisattva’s Inner Precepts Sūtra*, one fascicle, eighteen sheets;
*The Sūtra on the Dignified Conduct of the Five Lay Precepts for Upāsakas*, one fascicle, fifteen sheets;
*Mañjuśrī’s Sūtra on the Pure Vinaya*, one fascicle—also simply titled *The Sūtra on the Pure Vinaya*.
*The Extensive Scripture on the Purification of the Vinaya*, one fascicle, thirteen pages;
*The Scripture on the Questions of Śāntamati*, one fascicle, also titled *The Scripture on the Cool Subduing Spoken by the Tathāgata*, seventeen pages;
*The Mahāyāna Scripture on the Repentance of the Three Aggregates*, one fascicle, eighteen pages.
*The Bodhisattva’s Fivefold Repentance Text*, one fascicle (also titled *The Sūtra on the Bodhisattva’s Fivefold Repentance*), two sheets;
*The Bodhisattvapitaka Sūtra*, one fascicle, ten sheets; *The Samantabhadradhāraṇī Bodhisattva Sūtra*, one fascicle.
*The Sūtra on the Bodhisattva Receiving the Upavāsa*, one scroll, three pages;
*The Mañjuśrī Sūtra on Repenting of Transgressions*, one scroll, twenty-one pages—also titled *The Mañjuśrī Sūtra on Repenting with the Five Limbs*;
*The Śāriputra Sūtra on Repenting of Transgressions*, one scroll, also simply titled *The Sūtra on Repenting of Transgressions*.
*Wǔzhǐ Fǎlǜ Sānmèijīng* (Five-Sheet Scripture on the Samādhi of the Dharma-Regulations), one fascicle; also simply titled *Fǎlǜ*.
Seven sheets. *Shíshàn Yèdào Jīng* (Scripture on the Path of Ten Wholesome Actions), one fascicle.
Six sheets. The fourteen scriptures above, totaling fourteen fascicles, are contained in the same volume.
In total, there are one hundred and seventy-two sheets. Regarding Mahāyāna treatises:

ninety-nine works totaling five hundred and twenty fascicles, arranged in fifty bundles; and twenty-one works totaling one hundred and fifty-five fascicles of commentaries (*śāstra*). Regarding compendia of doctrine: seventy-eight works totaling three hundred and sixty-five fascicles.

The *Mahāprajñāpāramitā-śāstra* (Treatise on the Great Perfection of Wisdom) in one hundred fascicles—also called the *Mahāprajñāpāramitā-sūtra-śāstra*, the *Mahāprajñā-vyākhyā-śāstra*, or in versions of one hundred ten fascicles or seventy fascicles; ten bundles (*chì*); two thousand eighty-five sheets. The *Daśabhūmika-vibhāṣā-śāstra* (Treatise on the Ten Stages Sūtra) in twelve fascicles—or fifteen fascicles; one bundle; two hundred forty-six sheets. The *Maitreyaparipṛcchā-sūtra-śāstra* (Treatise on the Sūtra of the Questions of Maitreya Bodhisattva) in five fascicles—or six, seven, or ten fascicles; one hundred twenty-eight sheets. The *Ratnakūṭa-mahāyāna-sūtra-śāstra* (Treatise on the Mahāyāna Ratnakūṭa Sūtra) in four fascicles; eighty-four sheets. The *Ratnacūḍa-bodhisattva-caturdharma-sūtra-śāstra* (Treatise on the Sūtra of the Four Dharmas of Bodhisattva Ratnacūḍa), titled *Ratnacūḍa-sūtra-caturdharma-upadeśa*; one fascicle; twelve sheets. The three aforementioned treatises comprise ten fascicles in a single bundle, totaling two thousand five hundred fifty-five sheets.

*Fodi jing lun* (Treatise on the Buddha-bhūmi Sūtra), seven fascicles, one hundred and seventeen sheets. *Vajracchedikā-prajñāpāramitā-śāstra*, two fascicles, composed by Bodhisattva Asaṅga, thirty sheets. *Vajracchedikā-prajñāpāramitā-sūtra-śāstra-kārikā*, one fascicle, also known as the *Vajracchedikā-śāstra-kārikā*, four sheets. The above three treatises comprise ten fascicles in a single volume, totaling one hundred and fifty-one sheets.
*Vajracchedikā-prajñāpāramitā-śāstra*, three fascicles, composed by Bodhisattva Vasubandhu;
forty-eight sheets. *Vajracchedikā-prajñāpāramitā-sūtra-śāstra-vyākhyā*, also known as *Vajracchedikā-śāstra-vyākhyā*, three fascicles; thirty-three sheets.
*Vajracchedikā-prajñāpāramitā-sūtra-bhagna-grahaṇa-anabhedya-prajñapti-nāma-śāstra*, also known as the *Guṇaprabha-śāstra*, two fascicles.
The *Mañjuśrī-paripṛcchā-bodhicitta-śāstra* in two fascicles, also titled the *Mañjuśrī-paripṛcchā-bodhicitta-sūtra-śāstra*, or alternatively the *Gayāśīrṣa-sūtra-śāstra*, in thirty sheets;
and the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra-upadeśa*, titled the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra-śāstra*, in one fascicle and twenty-five sheets.
These five treatises, totaling eleven fascicles, are contained in the same volume.
The total comprises one hundred and sixty-nine folios.
The *Dharmapada-śāstra* (Treatise on the Lotus Sūtra) consists of two fascicles; the first contains a verse of homage, and it is sometimes recorded as a single fascicle.
It is also known as the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra-upadeśa*, comprising thirty folios. The *Vimalakīrti-nirdeśa-sūtra-śāstra* consists of four fascicles, or alternatively three fascicles.
*Mahāparinirvāṇa-śāstra*, one fascicle, fifty-nine pages; alternatively titled *Mahāparinirvāṇa-sūtra-śāstra*, ten pages;
*Nirvāṇa-sūtra-gāthā on Original Existence and Present Non-existence*, one fascicle, also simply titled *Original Existence and Present Non-existence*, six pages;
*Śāstra on the Sutra of the Bequeathed Teaching*, one fascicle.
*The Commentary on the Sūtra of Immeasurable Life*, one fascicle, twenty-six pages; titled *Upadeśa on the Sūtra of Immeasurable Life*, including the "Verses on the Vow for Rebirth," seven pages.
*The Commentary on the Sūtra of the Threefold Perfection*, one fascicle, eighteen pages; titled *Upadeśa on the Sūtra of the Threefold Perfection*.
*The Commentary on the Sūtra of Turning the Wheel of Dharma*, one fascicle; titled *Upadeśa on the Sūtra of Turning the Wheel of Dharma*.

The first ten scrolls consist of eight treatises totaling eleven fascicles in one bundle, comprising one hundred and sixty-six pages. The *Yogācārabhūmi-śāstra*, one hundred fascicles in ten bundles, comprises one thousand eight hundred and seventeen pages.

The *Prakaraṇāryavācā-śāstra*, twenty fascicles in two bundles, comprises three hundred and twenty-seven pages. The *Yogācārabhūmi-bhāṣya*, one fascicle, comprises nineteen pages. The *Prakaraṇāryavācā-kārikā*, one fascicle, comprises thirteen pages. The *Rājadharmasamyak-nirdeśa-śāstra*, one fascicle, comprises twenty pages. The *Mahāyānābhidharma-samuccaya-śāstra*, seven fascicles, comprises one hundred and three pages. These four aforementioned treatises total ten fascicles in one bundle, comprising two thousand two hundred and ninety-nine pages.

The *Mahāyānābhidharmasamuccayavyākhyā* (Great Vehicle Compendium of Abhidharma), sixteen fascicles, two hundred and fifty-five sheets; the *Madhyamaka-śāstra* (Treatise on the Middle Way), also known as the *Mādhyamika-śāstra*, four fascicles—or eight fascicles—ninety-eight sheets. These two treatises, totaling twenty fascicles, are contained in the same volume, comprising three hundred and fifty-three sheets in all.

The *Prajñāpradīpa-śāstra* (Exegesis on the Lamp of Wisdom), fifteen fascicles, two hundred fifty-two sheets; the *Dvādaśamukha-śāstra* (Treatise on the Twelve Gates), one fascicle, twenty-four sheets; the *Aṣṭadaśaśūnyatā-śāstra* (Treatise on the Eighteen Emptinesses), one fascicle, twenty sheets; the *Śata-śāstra* (Treatise in One Hundred [Verses]), two fascicles, forty-three sheets; the *Viśata-śāstra-mūla* (Root Text of the Extensive Treatise in One Hundred [Verses]), one fascicle, eight sheets. These five superior treatises comprise twenty fascicles in two bundles, totaling three hundred forty-seven sheets.

The *Mahāyāna-śataka-vṛtti* (Commentary on the Hundred Verses of the Mahāyāna), ten fascicles, one bundle; 197 sheets. The *Daśabhūmika-vibhāṣā-śāstra* (Treatise on the Elucidation of the Ten Stages), fourteen fascicles—sometimes titled with the character "wú" (without) or in twelve or fifteen fascicles; 276 sheets. The *Bodhicaryāvatāra-prajñāpāramitā-upadeśa-śāstra* (Treatise on the Equipment for Enlightenment), six fascicles; 67 sheets. The above two treatises comprise twenty fascicles and two bundles, totaling 540 sheets.

The Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra-śāstra, thirteen fascicles (or fifteen fascicles), one bundle; two hundred and five sheets. The Madhyamaka-anupūrvi-śāstra, two fascicles, titled *Madhyamaka-anupūrvi-śāstra-artha-praveśa-mahāprajñāpāramitā-sūtra*; thirty-two sheets. The Mahāyānasaṃgraha-śāstra, three fascicles, translated by Tripiṭaka Master Paramārtha; fifty-nine sheets. The aforementioned three treatises comprise twenty fascicles in two bundles, totaling five hundred and five sheets.

*Mahāyānasaṃgraha-śāstra*, two fascicles, translated by Buddhanta; forty-four pages. *Mahāyānasaṃgraha-bhāṣya*, three fascicles, translated by Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang; sixty-six pages. *Mahāyānasaṃgraha-bhāṣya-vyākhyā*, fifteen fascicles, commentary by Vasubandhu, translated by Paramārtha; alternatively in twelve fascicles, also titled *Vyākhyā-śāstra*; three hundred twenty-seven pages. The above three treatises comprise twenty fascicles in two volumes, totaling four hundred thirty-two pages.

*Mahāyānasaṃgrahabhāṣya* (Commentary on the Compendium of the Great Vehicle), ten fascicles; commentary by Vasubandhu, translated by Paramārtha. 156 sheets. *Mahāyānasaṃgrahabhāṣya*, ten fascicles; one set; commentary by Vasubandhu, translated by Xuanzang. 176 sheets. *Mahāyānasaṃgrahopanibandhana* (Sub-commentary on the Compendium of the Great Vehicle), ten fascicles; one set; commentary by Asvabhāva, translated by Xuanzang. 216 sheets. *Buddhadhātuśāstra* (Treatise on Buddha-nature), four fascicles. 83 sheets. *Niyatāniyatagotravyavasthāna-śāstra* (Treatise on the Determined and Undetermined Lineages), three fascicles. 53 sheets. *Madhyāntavibhāgakārikā* (Verses on the Discrimination of the Middle and the Extremes), one fascicle. 5 sheets. *Madhyāntavibhāga-bhāṣya* (Commentary on the Discrimination of the Middle and the Extremes), two or three fascicles. 38 sheets. The above four treatises comprise ten fascicles in a single set, totaling 727 sheets.

*Madhyāntavibhāga-bhāṣya* (Discourse on Distinguishing the Middle from the Extremes), three fascicles, thirty-nine sheets. *Ratnagotravibhāga-mahāyānottaratantra-śāstra* (Treatise on the Ultimate One Vehicle Jewel Nature), also known as *Ratnagotra-vibhāga* or *Mahāyānottaratantra*, four fascicles—or alternatively three or five fascicles—eighty sheets. *Karmasiddhi-prakaraṇa* (Treatise on the Achievement of Karma), one fascicle, twelve sheets. *Mahāyāna-karmasiddhi-śāstra* (Treatise on the Achievement of Karma in the Mahāyāna), one fascicle, seventeen sheets. *Nyāyamukha-śāstra* (Treatise on the Gateway to Logic), one fascicle, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang, fifteen sheets. The above five treatises, totaling ten fascicles, are contained in the same volume; they comprise one hundred and sixty-three sheets in all.
*Hetuvidyānyāyamukhaśāstra*, one fascicle, translated by Tripiṭaka Master Yijing;
sixteen sheets. *Hetuvidyāpraveśanyāyaśāstra*, one fascicle; six sheets.
*Vijñaptimātratāsiddhi-śāstra*, one fascicle, titled "Chapter on Manifesting Consciousness" (*Vijñaptiprakaraṇa*), excerpted from the *Nirākāra-śāstra*.
*Zhuan shi lun* (Treatise on the Transformation of Consciousness), one fascicle, nineteen sheets.

*Weishi lun* (Treatise on Consciousness-Only), one fascicle, three sheets; also titled *Po se xin* (Refuting Matter and Mind). The beginning states "Consciousness-only, no external objects," or it is called *Weishi wu jingjie lun* (Treatise on Consciousness-only Without External Objects).

Nineteen sheets. *Weishi lun* (Treatise on Consciousness-Only), one fascicle; the beginning states "Cultivating the Path Not Shared with Others," or it is called *Sheng weishi lun* (Vehicle of Consciousness-only Treatise).
*Vijñaptimātratāsiddhi-viṃśatikā-śāstra*, one fascicle, ten sheets;
*Vijñaptimātratāsiddhi-ratnasambhava-śāstra*, five fascicles (also titled *Triṃśikāvijñaptibhāṣya-anuvyākhyāna*), sixty-five sheets;
*Vijñaptimātratāsiddhi-triṃśikā-kārikā*, one fascicle, ten sheets.

The *Abhidharma-mahāvibhāṣā-śāstra*, two hundred fascicles; alternatively called the *Abhidharma-jñānaprasthāna-mahāvibhāṣā*; twenty bundles; three thousand six hundred and sixty-nine sheets. The *Abhidharmakośa-bhāṣya*, twenty-two fascicles (or without the character "Bhāṣya"); four hundred and seventy-one sheets. The *Abhidharmakośa-kārikā*, one fascicle (or three fascicles); twenty-three sheets. The above two treatises comprise twenty-three fascicles; three bundles: the first bundle contains seven fascicles, while the middle and lower bundles each contain eight fascicles.

*Abhidharmakośa-śāstra*, thirty fascicles; three bundles; four hundred and sixty-five sheets. *Abhidharmanyāyānusāra-śāstra*, eighty fascicles; eight bundles; one thousand three hundred and ninety-four sheets. *Abhidharmasamaya-pradīpikā-śāstra*, forty fascicles; four bundles; six hundred and fourteen sheets. *Dharmatrāta-abhidharma-hṛdaya-śāstra*, four fascicles (sometimes lacking the character "lun" [treatise]); sixty-nine sheets. *Abhidharma-hṛdaya-sūtra*, six fascicles (sometimes lacking the character "jing" [sūtra], sometimes lacking the name "Dharmatrāta," sometimes seven fascicles, or titled *Dharmatrāta-abhidharma-śāstra*, or with a separate translation added); one hundred and five sheets. The above two treatises, totaling ten fascicles, share the same bundle.

The *Saṃyuktābhidharmahṛdaya-śāstra* (Treatise on the Heart of Mixed Abhidharma), eleven fascicles—or sometimes without the word "treatise" (*śāstra*)—also called the *Saṃyuktābhidharma-sūtra* or the *Saṃyuktābhidharma-vibhāṣā*, or ten fascicles; four [cases], totaling two hundred and seventy-nine sheets. The *Abhidharmāmṛta-rasa-śāstra* (Treatise on the Flavor of the Ambrosia of Abhidharma), two fascicles—or called the *Amṛtarasa-abhidharma* or without the word "treatise"—forty-six sheets. The *Anuśaya-lakṣaṇa-śāstra* (Treatise on the Characteristics of Latent Tendencies), one fascicle—or called the *Guṇamati-anuśaya-lakṣaṇa-śāstra* or two fascicles—thirty-four sheets. The above three treatises comprise fourteen fascicles in two volumes.

The *Ācārya Vasumitra Bodhisattva-saṃgīti-śāstra* in ten fascicles, or twelve fascicles, or fourteen fascicles; also called the *Vasumitra-sūtra*. Total: 362 sheets. The *Tri-dharmaka-śāstra* in two fascicles; alternatively without the character "lun" (treatise), or called the *Sūtra-śāstra*, or in three fascicles, or called one fascicle. Total: 49 sheets. The *Abhidharma-praveśa-śāstra* in two fascicles. Total: 28 sheets. The above three treatises comprise fourteen fascicles in two bundles.

The *Tattvasiddhi-śāstra* (*Chengshi lun*) consists of twenty fascicles and comprises two hundred and two chapters; it is also found in versions of twenty-four, twenty-seven, fourteen, or sixteen fascicles, spanning two bundles and totaling three hundred and ninety-eight sheets.
The *Lokaprajñapti-abhidharma-śāstra* (*Lishi apitan lun*) consists of ten fascicles in one bundle;
its title is sometimes given as *Lishi abidanzang* (without the character "lun") or as fifteen fascicles, and it is also known as the *Tiandi ji jing* (Sutra on the Record of Heaven and Earth).
One fascicle containing one hundred and sixty-four sheets: *Vimuttimagga* (Treatise on the Path of Liberation), twelve or thirteen fascicles;

one fascicle containing one hundred and ninety-seven sheets: *Śāriputrābhidharma-śāstra* (Śāriputra’s Abhidharma Treatise), twenty-two fascicles—sometimes omitting the character "lun" (treatise)—or twenty or thirty fascicles.
The *Pañcavastu-vibhāṣā-śāstra* in two fascicles, consisting of 604 sheets, is also called the *Abhidharma-pañcavastu-śāstra* in twenty-four sheets;
these two treatises comprise twenty-four fascicles in three bundles.

The *Vibhāṣā-śāstra* in fourteen fascicles is also called the *Vibhāṣā-abhidharma-śāstra*, or the *Vyāsabhāṣya*; it is also in fifteen fascicles, nineteen fascicles, or lacks the character "lun" (treatise). It consists of three hundred and thirty-four sheets. The *Sammitīya-nikāya-śāstra* in three fascicles is sometimes without the character "bu" (nikāya), or is said to be in four fascicles; it consists of thirty-six sheets. The two aforementioned treatises comprise seventeen fascicles in two bundles: the first eight fascicles and the latter nine fascicles.

*Vibhaṅga-śāstra* (Treatise on the Analysis of Merit), four fascicles—also called *Vibhaṅga-sūtra*—or three or five fascicles; seventy-one sheets. *Catuḥsatya-śāstra* (Treatise on the Four Noble Truths), four fascicles; seventy-five sheets. *Pratyekabuddha-nidāna-śāstra* (Treatise on the Causes and Conditions of Pratyekabuddhas), two fascicles; twenty sheets. *Aṣṭādaśa-nikāya-śāstra* (Treatise on the Eighteen Schools), one fascicle; eight sheets. *Samayabhedoparacanacakra-śāstra* (Treatise on the Different Tenets of the Schools), one fascicle, also titled *Nikāyabheda-śāstra*; nine sheets. *Samayabhedoparacanacakra-śāstra*, one fascicle; eight sheets. These six aforementioned treatises, totaling thirteen fascicles, are contained in the same volume.

The *Collection of the Wise and Holy* (*Xian-sheng ji xian-sheng ji*) consists of one hundred and twelve works totaling six hundred and eighteen fascicles in seven bundles; sixty-eight works totaling one hundred and seventy-three fascicles translated from Sanskrit originals; forty-four works totaling four hundred and twenty-two fascicles compiled locally; and the *Buddhacarita-kāvya* (*Fo-suo-xing-zan jing-chuan*) in five fascicles—sometimes titled *Buddhacarita-kāvya* without the character "chuan" (transmission), sometimes titled *Chuan* without the character "jing" (sūtra), and also known as the *Buddha-pūrva-yoga-sūtra*—occupying ninety sheets. The *Buddha-pūrva-yoga-sūtra* in seven fascicles, also known as the *Buddha-pūrva-yoga-saṃgraha-sūtra*, occupies one hundred and thirteen sheets. The above two collections comprise twelve fascicles in a single bundle.

*Zhuanjibaiyuan jing* (Sūtra of One Hundred Compiled Avenues), ten fascicles; one bundle; one hundred and fifty sheets. *Chuyao jing* (Udānavarga), twenty fascicles—also called *Chuyao lun* (Treatise on the Manifestation of Light)—or nineteen fascicles; four hundred and eighty-four sheets. *Xianyu jing* (Sūtra of the Wise and the Foolish), thirteen fascicles—or fifteen, sixteen, or seventeen fascicles—also called *Xianyu yinyuan jing* (Sūtra of the Causes and Conditions of the Wise and the Foolish); two hundred and eighty-three sheets. The above two collections comprise thirty-three fascicles in four bundles; the first three bundles each contain eight fascicles.

The fourth bundle contains nine fascicles: *The Sūtra on the Stages of the Path* (Dàodì jīng), one fascicle; alternatively titled *The Great Sūtra on the Stages of the Path*. 18 sheets. *The Sūtra on the Practice of the Stages of the Path* (Xiūxíng dàodì jīng), six fascicles. The title of the first fascicle reads *Yujia fumi jīng*. In the Jin dynasty it was called *Xiūxíng dàodì jīng*, or simply *Xiūxíng jīng*, or in seven fascicles. 145 sheets. *Sūtra Compiled by Saṃgharakṣa* (Sēngqiéluóchā suójí jīng), three fascicles; alternatively titled *Saṃgharakṣa’s Collection* or in five fascicles. 85 sheets. The above three collections comprise ten fascicles in a single bundle.

*The Sutra of One Hundred Parables* (Baiyu jing), four fascicles, or five fascicles, or said to be ten fascicles; its details are unknown. It is also called *The Sutra of One Hundred Sentences of Parables*. [54 sheets] *The Sutra of the Original Conditions of the Bodhisattva* (Pusa benyuan jing), three fascicles; also called *The Compendium of the Original Deeds of the Bodhisattva* (Pusa benxing ji jing). It is also in two fascicles or four fascicles. [54 sheets] *The Essential Collection of Various Sutras on the Gate of Bodhisattva Practice in Mahayana Cultivation* (Dacheng xiuxing pusa xingmen zhu jing yaoji), three fascicles. [81 sheets] The above three collections comprise ten fascicles in one volume.
*The Transmission of the Dharma-treasury through Successive Causes and Conditions*, six fascicles (sometimes omitting the characters "causes and conditions," also called the *Dharma-treasury Sūtra*;

alternatively in four fascicles or two fascicles, eighty-two pages). *Sitting Meditation Samādhi Sūtra*, three fascicles (also known as the *Bodhisattva’s Dhyāna Method Sūtra*, or simply the *Dhyāna Sūtra*; also called the *Aranya Practice of Dhyāna Method Sūtra*;
alternatively in two fascicles, fifty pages). *Buddha-physician Sūtra*, one fascicle (also called the *Buddha-physician King Sūtra*).
*Wéirì záshì jīng* (Sūtra on Miscellaneous Matters for Each Day), one fascicle, fifteen sheets.

*Bófānníhuán móhégāshè fùfó jīng* (The Sūtra of the Buddha’s Parinirvāṇa and Mahākāśyapa’s Journey to the Buddha), one fascicle; also called *Gāshè fùbānníhuán jīng* (The Sūtra of Kāśyapa’s Journey to the Parinirvāṇa), two sheets.
*Púsà hèsèyù fǎ* (The Dharma of the Bodhisattva’s Rebuke of Form and Desire), one fascicle; also called a sūtra.
One scroll, four folios: *Xuefa jing* (Sūtra on the Study of the Dharma), or without the word "sūtra," two folios. One scroll, six folios:
*Furu niepan miju jin gang li shi ailian jing* (Sūtra on the Buddha’s Entry into Nirvāṇa and the Lamentation of the Secret-Trace Vajra-Mighty-Wielder).

One scroll, six folios: *Jiazhanyan shuofa moshu jie jing* (Sūtra on the Verses on the Extinction of Phenomena Spoken by Kātyāyana); the title reads "Verses on the Extinction of Phenomena Spoken by the Bhikṣu Kātyāyana, Sent by the Buddha," consisting of one hundred and twenty chapters; it is also simply called the *Kātyāyana Verses*.
*The Sutra on the Buddha’s Treatment of the Body*, five sheets; also known as *The Sutra on the Treatment of the Body*, one sheet.
*The Sutra on the Treatment of the Mind*, one sheet; also known as *The Buddha’s Sutra on the Mind*, one sheet.
These eleven collections, totaling eighteen fascicles, are contained in the same volume.

*Saṃyukta-ratnapiṭaka-sūtra*, eight fascicles (alternatively said to be thirteen fascicles), one hundred and fifty-three sheets; *Nāgasena-bhikṣu-sūtra*, two fascicles (alternatively called the *Nāgasena-sūtra* or three fascicles), thirty-one sheets. The above two collections comprise ten fascicles in a single volume.
*The Essential Methods for the Five-Gate Dhyāna Sūtra*, one fascicle, twenty-three sheets.

*Dharmatrāta’s Dhyāna Sūtra*, two fascicles; also titled *The Path of Practice in the Gaṅgā-Caraka*; also titled *The Sūtra on the Contemplation of Impurity*; also titled *The Sūtra on the Expedient Means of Cultivation*.
Fifty-one sheets. *The Essential Explanation of Dhyāna Methods*, two fascicles; titled *The Sūtra on the Essentials of Dhyāna*.
*The Thirty-Four Sheets of Essential Chan Teachings: The Sūtra on Rebuking Desire*, one fascicle (titled *The Essential Chan Teachings Sūtra, Chapter on Rebuking Desire*), four sheets;
*The Sūtra on Contemplating the Internal Body and Its Phrases*, one fascicle (or without phrases/characters), two sheets;
*The Sūtra on the Contemplation of Dharmas*, one fascicle.

Seven sheets. The *Aśoka-rāja-sūtra*, ten fascicles, one hundred and eleven sheets; the above four collections, fourteen fascicles, same volume.

*The Biography of King Aśoka* (A-yü-wang-chuan), seven fascicles—sometimes with the character "Da" (Great) prefixed, or five fascicles; also called the *Mahā-aśokarāja-sūtra*. Twenty-six sheets. *Annotated Excerpts from the Four Āgamas* (Sì-āhán-mù-chāo-jie), two fascicles; also called the *Sì-āhán-mù-chāo-jīng*. Forty-six sheets. The above three collections comprise ten fascicles in one volume.
The *Dharmapada-sūtra*, two fascicles; also called the *Dharmapada-saṃgraha*, thirty-four sheets.
The *Dharmapada-avadāna-sūtra*, four fascicles—also named the *Dharmapada-mūla-prakaraṇa-sūtra* or the *Dharmopama-sūtra*; alternatively in five or six fascicles, ninety-five sheets.
The *Kāśyapa-buddha-vyākaraṇa-sūtra*, one fascicle.

*Zuàn jí sānzàng jí zázàng chuán* (Biography of the Compilation of the Tripiṭaka and the Miscellaneous Piṭaka), one fascicle; also titled *Zuàn sānzàng jīng jí zázàng jīng* (Compilation of the Sūtras of the Tripiṭaka and the Sūtras of the Miscellaneous Piṭaka), eight sheets.
*Sānhuì jīng* (Sūtra on the Three Wisdoms), one fascicle, twelve sheets.

*Ekādaśa-patra Āgama-mukha-vyākhyāna-dvādaśāṅga-pratītyasamutpāda-sūtra*, one fascicle; also called *Dvādaśāṅga-pratītyasamutpāda-cchedaka-sūtra*, or *Āgama-mukha-vyākhyāna-sūtra*, eight pages.
*Kṣudra-mārga-bhūmi-sūtra*, one fascicle, four pages.
*Mañjuśrī-praṇidhāna-sūtra*, one fascicle; sometimes the character "verse" (*gāthā*) is added [to the title].
One scroll, two pages: *Names of Six Bodhisattvas*. The entry into the canon notes: "The names of the bodhisattvas should also be recited and maintained.
One scroll, one hundred and fifty pages: *Verses of Praise to the Buddha in One Hundred and Fifty Stanzas*.
Six scrolls: *Verses of Praise to Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva*. One scroll.
Four sheets: Fascicle 12, Volumes 16 [of the same collection], bound together in one bundle.
*Amūrta-rākṣasa-saṃgraha* (also called *Amūrta-rākṣasa-sūtra*), one fascicle, or two fascicles, twenty-two sheets.
*Bodhisattva Aśvaghoṣa-carita*, one fascicle.
One fascicle, three sheets: *Biography of Bodhisattva Nāgārjuna*.
One fascicle, three sheets: *Biography of Bodhisattva Āryadeva*. One fascicle, four sheets:
*Biography of Dharma Master Vasubandhu*; he is also called Tianqin (Devaputra).
*The Essential Verses on the Dharma Spoken by Bodhisattva Nāgārjuna for King Śāntaka*, one scroll, ten pages;
*The Essential Verses Exhorting All Kings*, one scroll, nine pages;
*Verses of Admonition to Kings by Bodhisattva Nāgārjuna*, one scroll, six pages.
*The Sūtra on Piṇḍola Bharadvāja Preaching the Dharma for King Udayana*, one fascicle (six sheets); also called *The Sūtra on Piṇḍola Preaching the Dharma for the King*, eight sheets.
*The Method for Inviting Piṇḍola*, one fascicle; also called *The Sūtra on the Method for Inviting Piṇḍola*, two sheets.

*A Brief Exposition on the Differentiation of Karmic Retribution*, one fascicle; also called *The Great Hero Bodhisattva’s Brief Exposition on the Differentiation of Karmic Retribution*, or *The Collected Brief Exposition on the Differentiation of Karmic Retribution*.

One fascicle of the *Jiading Biqiu Shuodanglai Bian Jing* (Sūtra on the Discourse of the Bhikṣu Jiading on Future Transformations), also simply called the *Jiading Biqiu Jing*, consisting of eight pages;
one fascicle of the *Dana-miduo Suoshuo Fazu Ji* (Record of the Dharma Abiding as Spoken by the Great Arhat Nandimitra), consisting of seven pages;
and three fascicles of the *Jin Qishi Lun* (Seventy Verses on Gold), also known as the *Sengqie Lun* (Sāṃkhya Treatise), also in three fascicles.
The *Daśapadārtha-śāstra* (Treatise on the Ten Categories), one fascicle, fifty-three pages;
the *Abhidharmasamuccaya*, seventeen fascicles, eleven pages. The above are translations from Indic manuscripts; the following are compilations by local [Chinese] authors.

*Mahābuddhanāmasūtra*, sixteen fascicles; two volumes. On the twenty-third day of the tenth month of the fifteenth year of the Zhenyuan era, by imperial decree, it was entered into the catalog. The titles on the fascicle covers simply read *Buddhanāmasūtra*. The above three collections comprise thirteen fascicles: seven in the upper volume and six in the lower volume, totaling two volumes.

*Jīnglù yìxiàng* (Diverse Phenomena of Sūtras and Vinaya), fifty fascicles, five bundles, eight hundred twenty-seven sheets. *Dáluóní zájí* (Miscellaneous Collection of Dhāraṇīs), ten fascicles, one bundle, one hundred eighty-eight sheets. *Zhūjīng yàojí* (Essential Collection from Various Sūtras), twenty fascicles—or thirty fascicles—five hundred eighty-two sheets. The *Chusanzangjiji* (Collection of Records Concerning the Translation of the Tripitaka), fifteen fascicles, three hundred and fourteen sheets; the *Zhongjingmulu* (Catalogue of All Scriptures), seven fascicles, sixty-three sheets; the aforementioned two collections comprise twenty-two fascicles in two bundles: the upper bundle contains ten fascicles, and the lower bundle contains twelve fascicles.

The *Dàtáng nèidiǎn lù* (Record of Buddhist Scriptures of the Great Tang), ten fascicles; one bundle, two hundred and twenty sheets. The *Xù gōngjīn yìjīng tújì* (Continuation of the Illustrated Account of the Translation of Scriptures from Antiquity to the Present), one fascicle, sixteen sheets. The *Kaiyuan Shijiao Lu* (Record of the Buddhist Teachings Compiled during the Kaiyuan Era), twenty fascicles in three volumes, is contained in this same volume [with the preceding work]. The *Xu Kaiyuan Shijiao Lu* (Continued Record of the Buddhist Teachings Compiled during the Kaiyuan Era), three fascicles, consists of seventy-five sheets. *Da Tang Xi Yu Ji* (Records of the Western Regions of the Great Tang), twelve fascicles, 234 sheets. *Ji Gu Jin Fo Dao Lun Heng* (Collected Weighings of Buddhist and Daoist Debates from Antiquity to the Present), four fascicles—or three fascicles—99 sheets. *Xu Ji Gu Jin Fo Dao Lun Heng* (Continued Collection of Weighings of Buddhist and Daoist Debates from Antiquity to the Present), one fascicle, 23 sheets. *Shang San Ji* (Three Collections, Upper Volume), seventeen fascicles, two bundles; the upper bundle contains eight fascicles, and the lower bundle contains nine fascicles.

*The Biography of the Tripitaka Master of Ci’en Monastery of the Great Tang*, ten fascicles; one bundle; one hundred and seventy sheets. *The Record of Eminent Monks Who Sought the Dharma in the Western Regions of the Great Tang*, two fascicles; thirty-five sheets. *The Biography of Faxian* (also titled *A Record of Travels through India*), one fascicle; twenty-nine sheets. *The Biographies of Eminent Monks*, fourteen fascicles; one fascicle is a table of contents; two hundred and ninety sheets. *Continued Biographies of Eminent Monks*, thirty fascicles, totaling seven hundred and thirty sheets; the first collection consists of thirty fascicles, divided into four bundles: the first and second bundles each contain eight fascicles, while the latter two bundles each contain seven.

*The Newly Compiled Catalogue of Śākyamuni’s Teachings from the Zhenyuan Era*, Volume 30: Subsequent List of Works Not Included in the Canon.
*The Scripture on the Vajrapāṇi Guhyapada* (7 fascicles, or 5 fascicles); *The Scripture on the Bodhisattva’s Dream*;

*The Scripture on the Dharma-nature of Non-differentiation of the Dharmadhātu as Spoken by the Śuddhāvāsakāyika Devaputra* (formerly titled *The Scripture on the Assembly of the Śuddhāvāsakāyika Devaputra*); *The Ten Dharmas*.
One fascicle of the *Sūtra*, with the title added as the *Mahāyāna Daśadharmaparivarta*; twenty fascicles of the *Mahāsattvasaṃghāṭasūtra*;
two fascicles of the *Buddhabhāṣitanandagarbhāvakrāntinirdeśasūtra*, renamed the *Garbhāvakrāntiparivarta*;
three fascicles of the *Mañjuśrīvyākaraṇasūtra*; and sixteen fascicles—or fourteen fascicles—of the *Bodhisattvadarśanatatvasamādhisūtra*.
The *Saṃyuktāgama* in three fascicles was renamed the *Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra-parivarta*. The *Rāṣṭrapālaparipṛcchā-sūtra* in two fascicles;
the *Ugraparipṛcchā-sūtra* in one fascicle; the *Kāśyapa-sūtra* in two fascicles, with the title expanded to the *Mahākāśyapa-parivarta*;
the *Arthavargiya-paripṛcchā-sūtra* in two fascicles; the *Abhayamati-dārikā-sūtra* in one fascicle; and the *Vimaladattā-bodhisattvā-sūtra*.
*Fenbie yingbian jing* (Discrimination and Elucidation Sutra), one fascicle; *Dafangdeng shanzhuyitianzi wenjing* (Mahāvaipulya Sutra on the Questions of the Devaputra Susthitamati), four fascicles;

*Dasheng fangbian jing* (Mahāyāna Sutra on Skillful Means), three fascicles; *Yishijing* (Sutra on the Transference of Consciousness), two fascicles—renamed *Xianhu changzhe hui* (Assembly of the Elder Bhadrapāla);
*Dafangdeng shanzhuyitianzi wenjing*, four fascicles; *Mile pusa suowen jing* (Sutra on the Questions of Maitreya Bodhisattva), one fascicle—renamed.
The *Mahāratnakūṭa Sūtra*, Chapter on Maitreya’s Questions on the Eight Dharmas, one fascicle; renamed as the *Puming Pusa Hui* (Assembly of the Bodhisattva Samantaprabha), two fascicles;
and the *Baoji Pusa Suowen Jing* (Sūtra of the Questions of the Bodhisattva Ratnaśikhin), two fascicles.
The above, from the *Miji Lishi Jing* (Sūtra of the Secret-Knower Vajrapāṇi) down, comprise twenty-three sections totaling eighty-four fascicles.
These have been incorporated into the *Mahāratnakūṭa-sūtra* collection;
therefore, no separate editions exist.
The *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtra* consists of seven fascicles or six fascicles in twenty-two chapters. The above two works comprise ten fascicles in total.
Its wording does not differ from the eight-fascicle version held in the Tripiṭaka.
Since that eight-fascicle version contains the complete number of chapters,
it was retained and included in the canon.
Because both of these [versions] were deficient, they were not retained.
The eight-fascicle version contains twenty-four chapters.
As for the new *Daoxing jing* in seven or ten fascicles, upon examining various editions in the Tripitaka, their texts are identical, yet the titles differ.
Because they are distinct, I have not transcribed them separately as the original text of the *Daoxing* (Practice of the Way). Upon searching for it, I have not yet obtained it.
The eight fascicles of the *Mahāvaipulya Mahāsaṃnipāta Sūtra* are actually combined with the sixth bundle of the *Mahāsaṃnipāta Sūtra*;

the current separate edition consists of the first two fascicles, which are the *Prajñāpāramitā Pañcāśatsahasrasaṃgraha-sūtra*, and the following six fascicles, which are the *Akṣayamati Anavatapta-nāgarāja Sūtra*.
The two fascicles [of this text] are identical in wording to the *Sūtra on the Extensive Manifestation of the Samādhi of the Middle Way* (*Zhongdao guangxian sanmei jing*) contained in the canon;

the three fascicles of the *Sūtra on the Divine Footsteps* (*Daoshen zu jing*) are identical in wording to the *Sūtra on the Infinite Transformations of the Divine Footsteps of the Way* (*Daoshenzu wuji bianhua jing*) contained in the canon;

the three fascicles of the *Sūtra of Lamentation* (*Aiqi jing*) are identical in wording to the *Vaipulya Mahāparinirvāṇa Sūtra* (*Fangdeng baniniyuan jing*) contained in the canon; and the *Ratnabuddhi-mudrā* [is likewise].
The *Mei jing* (One Scroll) is identical in wording to the *Huiyin sanmei jing* found in the Canon;
the *Luzi jing* (One Scroll) is identical in wording to the *Lumujing* found in the Canon; the *Xiao wuliangshou jing* (One Scroll) is identical in wording to the *Amituo jing* found in the Canon;
and the *Taizang jing* (One Scroll) is identical in wording to the *Wugouxian [jing]* found in the Canon.
The *Nü jīng* (Sutra on Women) is identical in its textual phrasing to the *Wénchéng shíèr yīnyuán jīng* (Sutra on the Twelve Links of Dependent Origination Heard in the City), one fascicle;

it is identical in its textual phrasing to the *Bēiduōshù xià sīwéi shíèr yīnyuán jīng* (Sutra on Contemplating the Twelve Links of Dependent Origination under the Peepal Tree) contained in the Canon;

the *Dà ānbān jīng* (Sutra on Great Anapanasati) is identical in its textual phrasing to the first fascicle of the *Dà ānbān shǒuyì jīng* (Sutra on the Guarding of Mindfulness through Anapanasati) contained in the Canon; and the *Shēnrì jīng* (Sutra on Shenri) is identical [in its textual phrasing] to... one fascicle.

The *Moonlight Youth Sūtra* (Yuèguāng tóngzǐ jīng) found in the [Chinese] canon is identical in wording and phrasing to the *Sūtra on the Rebirths in the Five Realms and the Retribution of Sin and Merit* (Lúnzhuǎn wúdào zuìfú bàoyìng jīng), one fascicle;
it is identical in wording and phrasing to the *Caṇḍāla Sūtra* (Zhēnduōyuè jīng) found in the [Tibetan] canon;

and it is identical in wording and phrasing to the *Sūtra of King Caṇḍāla* (Zhēnduōyuè guówáng jīng) found in the [Tibetan] canon; and there is also the *Sūtra of Authentic and Spurious Śramaṇas* (Zhēnwěi shā mén jīng), one fascicle.
The *Zhuanfalu jing* (Sūtra on Turning the Wheel of Dharma) in one fascicle is identical in wording to the *Kāśyapa-śīla-sūtra* found in the Tripiṭaka;
however, upon examining various versions of the canon, this is actually the *Dharmacakra-pravartana-śāstra*, which differs entirely from the *Dharmacakra-pravartana-sūtra*.
The *Pin-tou-lu wei wang shuo fa jing* (Sūtra on Piṇḍola Preaching the Dharma for the King) in one fascicle corresponds to the *Piṇḍola-bharadvāja-udāyana-rāja-sūtra* found in the Tripiṭaka.
The *Dharmapada-sūtra* (Fashuo jingwenju) is identical in its phrasing to the two-fascicle *Āraṇyaka-dhyāna-sūtra* (Aranuoxi channa fa jing).

It is also identical in its phrasing to the *Dhyāna-samādhi-sūtra* (Zuochan sanmei jing) found in the canon. As for the five-fascicle *Dhyānaguhya-uttama-sūtra* (Chan biyao jing), upon examining various versions in the canon, it was found that the text had entered an extreme state of corruption;
it is not the original scripture and is unfit for circulation. Although the authentic version of this scripture has been sought, it has not yet been obtained. [End of] New [Additions].
The *Dàoxíng* (Practice of the Way) and other works comprise nineteen sections totaling forty-two fascicles.
Some are single scriptures with multiple titles,
while others lack original manuscripts.
Therefore, one scripture from each has been retained, while duplicates have not been recorded.

*The Scripture on the Virtuous Woman Abhayā*, one fascicle; *The Scripture on the Supreme Dharma of the First Principle*, one fascicle; *The Scripture on the Original Vows Asked by Maitreya Bodhisattva*, one fascicle; *The Scripture on Arousing the Bodhicitta*, two fascicles—also known as the *Treatise on the Dharmapada*, two fascicles; and the *Commentary on the Mahāyānasaṃgraha*, twelve fascicles (or fifteen fascicles). These six works, totaling nineteen fascicles, are hereby recorded together for inclusion in the canon.
Two copies were previously carried [to China], and now only one remains.
The *Ākāśagarbha-paripṛcchā-sūtra* in eight fascicles—or five fascicles—is the complete single chapter on the *Ākāśagarbha-vastu* from the *Mahāsaṃnipāta-sūtra*.
The *Ākāśagarbha-bodhisattva-paripṛcchā-dhāraṇī-sūtra* in one fascicle is an excerpt from the aforementioned [text].
*The Sūtra on the Perfection of Giving Practiced by All Donors as Taught in the Śūnyatā-kośa*, one fascicle; an excerpt from the *Ṣaṭpāramitā-samuccaya* concerning the Perfection of Giving;
*The Mahāvaipulya Tathāgatagarbha-abhisambodhi-guhyakośa Sūtra*, two fascicles—this is the complete "Tathāgatagarbha-abhisambodhi" chapter from the old version of the *Avataṃsaka*;
*The Sūtra on Rebirth According to One’s Vows*, one fascicle; the old [version of the] *Bhaiṣajyaguru*.
*The Scripture on the Master* (一卷), one fascicle; this is the eleventh fascicle of the *Guǎngdìng jīng* (*Scripture of Consecration*), corresponding to the section "The Buddha’s Travel to Vaiśālī.
*The Scripture on the Vajrapāṇi Guhyapada* (密迹金剛力士經) (二卷), two fascicles; these are extracted from the fourth and fifth fascicles of the five-fascicle *Mìjī jīng*.
*The Scripture on the Increase by One* (增一阿含經) (一卷), one fascicle; this is extracted from the *Zēngyī Āhán Jīng*.
*The Sūtra on the Sevenfold Manifest Retribution in the Twenty-first Chapter*, one fascicle; excerpted from the *Ekottarika Āgama*, Chapter Twenty-one.
*The Sūtra on the Twelve Links of Dependent Origination*, one fascicle; excerpted from the *Ekottarika Āgama*, Chapter Sixteen.
*The Sūtra on Dharmas Corresponding to the Precepts*, one fascicle; excerpted from the *Saṃyukta Āgama*, Fascicle Thirty. *A Bhikṣu Questions the Buddha Concerning Many Matters*.
*The Sūtra on the Life-End of a Layman*, one fascicle; excerpted from the *Saṃyukta Āgama*, fascicle thirty. *The Sūtra on the Wealthy Householder*, one fascicle;
excerpted from the *Saṃyukta Āgama*, fascicle forty-six. *The Sūtra on Sentient Beings Committing Evil in the Three Times*, one fascicle;
excerpted from the *Udānavarga*, fascicle eight. *The Sūtra on the Merit of Leaving Home*; when the Buddha was at [Kāśī]...
The *Lántuó Zhúyuán* (Nālandā Bamboo Garden) is an excerpt from the "Chapter on the Merit of Leaving Home" (*Chūjiā Gōngdé Pǐn*) of the *Xiányú Jīng* (Sutra of the Wise and the Foolish).
It comprises fifteen sections and twenty-four fascicles, descending from the *Xūkōngzàng* (Ākāśagarbha).
Since it flows forth from this great scripture, [it is authoritative].
These are separate translations.
According to the catalogs of various scriptures, those that are separate translations need not be transcribed;
therefore, the catalogs of the Tripitaka excluded them and did not include them.

The *Makara-matsya-nidāna-sūtra*, one fascicle; the *Venerable Udāyin Leads the People to Pay Homage to the Buddha and the Saṃgha*, one fascicle; the *Returning to One’s Native Land to Save the Father King*, one fascicle; the *Sujāta-kumāra-sūtra*, one fascicle; the *Sūtra on Giving Things that are Lawful or Unlawful*, one fascicle; the *Sūtra of Instruction to Rāhula*, one fascicle; the *Sūtra on the Wheel of Birth and Death in the Five Destinies*, one fascicle; the *Sūtra on the Causes and Conditions of the Bhikṣu Svāgata*, one fascicle; the *Sūtra on the Seven Meritorious Deeds with and without Objects*, one fascicle; and the nine subsequent sūtras of the *Makara-matsya-nidāna*.
These are all extracted from the *Mūlasarvāstivāda-vinaya*:
the two-fascicle *Kulaputro Jyotiṣka-vipākavastu-sūtra*, the one-fascicle *Bhadanta Subhūti-kalyāṇasvara-sūtra*,
the one-fascicle *Pañca-jalaparissāvana-sūtra*, the one-fascicle *Vimalakīrti-devī-pūrvayoga-sūtra*, and the *Prasenajit-rāja-buddha-prasāda-sūtra*.
*The Sūtra on the Retribution for the Slaughter of the Śākya Clan*, one fascicle; *The Sūtra on the Great Mistress Bhikṣuṇī Entering Nirvāṇa*, two fascicles;
*The Sūtra on Sacrificing the Body out of Reverence for the Dharma*, one fascicle; *The Sūtra on Delivering Two Boys with False Views and Attaining the Fruit*, one fascicle;

*The Scripture on the Manifestation of Great Auspicious Omens at Birth*, one fascicle; *The Scripture on the Crossing of Kātyāyana*, one fascicle;
*The Scripture on the Karmic Retribution and Causes and Conditions of the Nāga King Elāpattra*, one fascicle; *The Scripture on the Causes and Conditions of Lady Anurādhā*, one fascicle;

*The Scripture on the Causes and Conditions of Puṣkarasārin*, three fascicles; *The Scripture on the Causes and Conditions of Prabhāsa*, one fascicle; and *The Manifestation of Great Supernatural Powers to Subdue Non-Buddhists*.
*Sūtra* (one fascicle); *The Sūtra on the Skillful Means of Mahābhaiṣajya* (two fascicles); *The Sūtra on the Buddha Descending from Heaven to Jambudvīpa* (one fascicle);
*The Sūtra of the Emaciated Kautamī* (one fascicle); *The Sūtra on the Causes and Conditions of Hārītī* (one fascicle);
*The Sūtra on the Nun Dharmadinnā Attaining the Fruit While Remaining a Laywoman* (one fascicle); *The Sūtra on the Arrogance of the Brahmin Vṛkṣaputra*; [and] *The Sūtra on the Younger Brother*.

*The Discourse on a Disciple Serving His Teacher*, one fascicle; *The Sūtra of the Seven Kinds of Non-Retrogression*, one fascicle; *The Discourse on Heedlessness Spoken by the Buddha for an Elder*, one fascicle;
*The Discourse on the Causes and Conditions of Earthquakes*, one fascicle; *The Discourse on the Four Seals of Black and White Dharmas*, one fascicle;
*The Discourse on the Buddha’s Imminent Entry into Nirvāṇa and His Deliverance of the Venerable Subhadra*, two fascicles; *The Announcement of the Minister Caraka upon the Parinirvāṇa of the Buddha*.
The *Rājan-sūtra*, one fascicle; the *Sūtra on the Division of Relics by Eight Great Kings*, one fascicle;
and the thirty-two sūtras beginning with the *Sūtra of the Householder Agnidatta*; all of these are extracted from the *Mūlasarvāstivāda-vinaya-kṣudraka-vastu*.
From the *Makara-jātaka-sūtra* down to forty-one works in forty-seven fascicles,
all of these were excerpted and circulated by Yi Jing from the *Nidāna-piṭaka* within the Vinaya of the Sarvāstivāda school.
Since these belong to a different category of beings, they are also not included in the formal catalog.

One fascicle of the *Āḍakavatsa-māyākāra-mantra-sūtra*, four fascicles of the *Ratnakūṭa-śāstra*, and four fascicles of the *Ratnagotravibhāga-śāstra*—these three works concerning the illusionist comprise nine fascicles in total.
It was also included in the *Zhou lu* (Catalogue of the Zhou Dynasty) among the scriptures seen in the imperial collection; however,
as I have searched for the original text and have not yet obtained it,
it is not recorded in this catalogue.
Regarding those newly translated scriptures for which the original Indic manuscripts have not been obtained, they cannot be recorded in full detail.

These include: the *Sukhāvatīvyūha-samādhi-sūtra* in three fascicles; the *Dharmadūta-sūtra* in two fascicles; the *Vīra-samādhi-sūtra* in two fascicles; the *Niścaya-puṇyapāpa-sūtra* in one fascicle; the *Upakāra-mati-sūtra* in two fascicles; the *Ārakṣa-jīvita-paritrāṇa-rogaduḥkha-vipatti-sūtra* in one fascicle; the *Parama-praṇīta-samādhi-sūtra* in one fascicle; the *Avalokiteśvara-samādhi-sūtra* in one fascicle; the *Viśuddha-dharmacaryā-sūtra* in one fascicle; the *Gao-wang-avalokiteśvara-sūtra* in one fascicle; and the *Viśuddha-pariṇāma-sūtra*. These ten sections comprise fifteen fascicles in total.
These are all spurious and doubtful scriptures found within ancient catalogs.
Although the Zhou catalog included them in its main body of texts,
their principles are all tainted by human contrivance.
Therefore, these have been excluded and not recorded in this catalogue.
Altogether, there are one hundred and eighteen works in two hundred and forty-seven fascicles;
most of these are already included in the various catalogues of the canon.
Now, as these are all cumbersome and prolix,
and some have been sought after but not yet obtained,
they are therefore not included among the number of established views.
Fearing that you may not know the details, I have briefly recounted them here.
If you wish to understand the origins in full detail,
they are all extensively described in the *Śanfan lu* (Record of the Elimination of Redundancies).
